articles.title: Tesla celebra Halloween con dos pasajeros de ultratumba en un coche sin conductor
articles.standfirst: La marca de Elon Musk ha puesto a circular por las calles de Austin un Cybercab autónomo con dos esqueletos en su interior. Una forma muy particular de celebrar la noche más terrorífica del año.
articles.summary: La marca de Elon Musk ha puesto a circular por las calles de Austin un Cybercab autónomo con dos esqueletos en su interior. Una forma muy particular de celebrar la noche más terrorífica del año.
articles.body: Los muertos han vuelto a la vida en Texas. O al menos se han dado una vuelta en coche. Tesla ha decidido celebrar Halloween de una forma bastante particular: paseando a dos esqueletos por las calles de Austin a bordo de uno de sus nuevos Cybercab, el taxi autónomo de la marca de Elon Musk que no necesita conductor para circular. La imagen resulta tan divertida como inquietante. Porque los dos siniestros pasajeros viajan en los únicos asientos disponibles en el coche, sin nadie al volante. De hecho, no podría haberlo: el Cybercab está diseñado para circular de forma autónoma y no tiene volante ni pedales. Los dos ocupantes de ultratumba tampoco han descuidado su seguridad: viajan con los cinturones abrochados. Y la iluminación ambiental del interior del Cybercab ayuda a crear una atmósfera todavía más tenebrosa, perfecta para la fiesta de Halloween. Tesla ha compartido esta peculiar iniciativa en las redes sociales de su servicio Robotaxi, convirtiendo a su vehículo autónomo en uno de los protagonistas más inesperados de la noche de los muertos. Aunque Halloween tiene sus raíces en antiguas celebraciones europeas, Estados Unidos ha convertido esta fiesta en un fenómeno mundial al que se suman cada vez más empresas. Tesla ha encontrado una forma de participar aprovechando una de las características más llamativas de su nuevo coche: que puede circular sin ningún ser humano a bordo. Habrá quien tema al Cybercab no sólo por los esqueletos que van dentro (al menos en esa unidad concreta) sino porque no confíe en su tecnología de conducción autónoma. Los datos deberían quitarnos ese miedo ya que, si nos ceñimos solo a Texas, hay más de 1.200 robotaxis de la marca de Elon Musk (entre los Cybercab y los Model Y autónomos) prestando este servicio. Según la NHTSA (la autoridad del tráfico en EE.UU.) se han registado 36 incidentes con ellos, con únicamente dos en los que ha habido lesiones. Nadie ha muerto a bordo de uno de ellos.

articles.title: ¡Nadie les baja del trono! Coello y Tapia sellan su cuarto año como número uno
articles.standfirst: Los 'Golden Boys' arrollan a Juan Tello y Maxi Arce por un doble 6-1 y aseguran matemáticamente el número uno mundial
articles.summary: Los Golden Boys arrollan a Juan Tello y Maxi Arce por un doble 6-1 y aseguran matemáticamente el número uno mundial
articles.body: Hay reinados que se sostienen y otros que se reinventan para seguir siendo eternos. Arturo Coello y Agustín Tapia pertenecen a esta segunda categoría. En Kuwait volvieron a demostrar que su dominio no entiende de calendarios ni de adversarios y conquistaron un nuevo Major con una exhibición incontestable ante Juan Tello y Maxi Arce. Un doble 6-1 para cerrar una final sin concesiones, sin titubeos y sin permitir que la pareja revelación del torneo pudiera siquiera soñar con discutirles el título. Pero el triunfo llevaba mucho más premio que un trofeo: los ‘Golden Boys’ certifican matemáticamente que terminarán 2026 como números uno del mundo. Cuatro años consecutivos en la cima. La final enfrentaba a dos realidades muy diferentes. En un lado, la pareja que ha marcado una época y que llegaba a Kuwait con una racha de 22 victorias consecutivas. En el otro, Juan Tello y Maxi Arce, la gran revelación del torneo, pareja número nueve del ranking y protagonistas de una semana extraordinaria. Para Arce, además, la cita tenía un significado especial: disputaba su primera final de Premier Padel. Sin embargo, la ilusión y el hambre de los aspirantes chocaron de frente con una maquinaria que funciona a una velocidad difícil de igualar. Coello y Tapia no estaban dispuestos a conceder ni un centímetro. Desde el primer intercambio, los número uno impusieron las condiciones. No hubo espacio para que Tello y Arce encontraran confianza, ni tiempo para que pudieran instalarse en el partido, y todo terminó con un doble 6-1. El triunfo eleva a 13 la cuenta de títulos de Coello y Tapia esta temporada. Se quedan a uno de igualar su mejor registro, los 14 trofeos conquistados en 2024, y prolongan una racha que ya alcanza las 22 victorias consecutivas. No pierden desde los cuartos de final del P1 de Madrid, durante la primera semana de septiembre. Desde entonces, torneo tras torneo, han convertido la recta final del calendario en una demostración de autoridad. En Kuwait, además, han puesto el sello definitivo a una temporada que ya tiene una certeza matemática: volverán a terminar en lo más alto del ranking mundial. Será su cuarto año consecutivo como números uno, una hegemonía que comenzó en 2023 y que confirma la dimensión de una pareja que ha sabido mantenerse en la cima sin dejar de evolucionar. La competencia cambia, los rivales se renuevan y las nuevas generaciones llaman a la puerta, pero Coello y Tapia siguen encontrando la manera de defender su territorio. Su dominio no se explica únicamente por los títulos, sino por la sensación de superioridad que transmiten cuando alcanzan su mejor versión. En las grandes citas, cuando el margen de error desaparece, parecen crecer todavía más. Kuwait deja también un nuevo hito individual para Agustín Tapia, que alcanza los 66 títulos en su carrera e iguala a Pablo Lima como el tercer jugador con más trofeos de la historia. Otro registro para una trayectoria que sigue escribiendo páginas extraordinarias y que, junto a la de Coello, ha construido uno de los binomios más dominantes que ha conocido este deporte. El reinado continúa. Y los reyes, lejos de conformarse, siguen ganando como si todavía tuvieran todo por conquistar.

articles.title: ClutchPoints’ Preseason 2026-27 College Basketball Top 25 Power Rankings
articles.summary: The 2026-27 college basketball season is upon us! Michigan comes in as the defending champions, but there has been plenty of upheaval with them. After winnin...
articles.body:
The 2026-27 college basketball season is upon us! Michigan comes in as the defending champions, but there has been plenty of upheaval with them. After winning their first title since 1989, Dusty May left for the Dallas Mavericks. Now, Michigan comes in as a Top 25 team, but not the favorite this year . Meanwhile, teams such as Duke come in with amazing freshman classes, while Florida brings back a ton of experience.

There are also the usual host of subjects expecting to contend again this year. Dan Hurley is looking to bring UConn back to a title, while Coen Carr leads Tom Izzo's Michigan State squad. Kelvin Sampson expects another dominant year from his Houston team as well. There are also the smaller teams that can surprise. Creighton has slowly built back to contending in the Big East, but still has to deal with Marquette and St. John's. Meanwhile, Grand Canyon is in its second season in the Mountain West and looks to make a run this season.

The 2026-27 season will open on Sunday, November 1, as Notre Dame and Villanova face off in Rome . Then, a college basketball fan's dream kicks off just at midnight Eastern time. It starts with Liberty facing High Point before a 24-hour frenzy of opening games. Everyone from Mercer to Duke, Maine to Illinois, will take to the court. With the season starting, it is time to look at the first power rankings of the season.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

No one has the depth that Duke has. They have an elite starting five, with a mix of experience and youth. John Blackwell comes in from Wisconsin, where he averaged 19.1 points per game and added another 5.1 rebounds per game. They also have Caleb Foster, another senior, who is expected to fight with Cayden Boozer for a starting guard spot. There is youth as well. Cameron Williams, the seven-foot-tall forward, has high expectations after choosing Duke over teams such as Arizona, Texas, and SMU. Meanwhile, Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje is expected to come off the bench. The 7-foot-2 big man who has played for FC Barcelona brings quality experience and size to the lineup. The backcourt is amazing, as is the frontcourt. Further, the depth is unlike anything else in college basketball, giving them the top rank to start the year. Duke opens their season on Monday hosting Army, before contests with Coastal Carolina and Michigan State.

Florida won the national championship in 2025 and still has some of those players on the roster. After a disappointing exit in the second round last season, expectations are high for Florida in 2026-27. The Gators are returning nearly 80 percent of their production from last year. Only Xaivian Lee and Micah Handlogten are gone. Meanwhile, Thomas Haugh, Alex Condon, Boogie Fland, and Rueben Chinyelu all return. Further, they bring in Denzel Aberdeen from Kentucky. Aberdeen was part of that championship team, but transferred to Kentucky last year, and is now back. The biggest concern is three-point shooting. While they won the SEC last year, the three-point shooting was horrible. The return of Aberdeen, who hit 62 3-pointers last year, should help that. Florida kicks off their campaign with a tough test, facing off with Miami on Monday before games with Jacksonville and Florida State.

Illinois made a run to the Final Four last year and brings back a loaded roster. They lost leading scorer Keton Wagler, as well as Kylan Boswell, but still have a ton coming back. David Mirkovic and Andrej Stojakovic were both pre-season All-Big Ten Selections, but Mirkovic will miss the start of the regular season due to offseason foot surgery . Meanwhile, they bring in Stefan Vaaks from Providence, who averaged 15.8 points per game. Illinois also has highly touted freshman Quentin Coleman, who has already been named to the Jerry West Award watch list . This team is set to make a run in the Big Ten and potentially further. They open their season on Monday, with games against Penn and Texas Tech on the schedule.

Brayden Burries, Koa Peat, and Jaden Bradley are all in the NBA now, which left some holes in the Arizona roster. Still, Motiejus Krivas and Ivan Kharchenkov are back. Krivas averages 8.2 rebounds per game with 10.4 points per game. Meanwhile, Kharchenkov also has 10.4 points per game with 4.3 rebounds and 2.3 assists. Derek Dixon and RJ Godfrey come in through the transfer portal and should add some solid scoring. Meanwhile, Caleb Holt is projected as a top prospect in the next NBA Draft, and the 5-star freshman is looking to make a splash in his first campaign with Arizona. The Wildcats open the season on Monday night against UCLA, before games against Cal Poly and Northern Illinois.

Michigan State did not look their best in the exhibition season, but expect Tom Izzo to have this team ready to go. It is one of the deepest teams in the nation, with 12 players who could see legitimate time on the court. They also have the star power to back up a high ranking. Jeremy Fears is back and has been named the preseason Big Ten Player of the Year . Fears averaged 15.2 points per game with 9.4 assists last year. They also have Jasiah Jervis, a highly touted freshman who could compete for a starting job. If Michigan State wants to make a run to the Final Four, which is being played in Detroit, Jervis is going to need to step up. They open up their season on Monday against Quinnipiac before games with Toledo and Duke.

Dan Hurley just got a nice contract extension and is looking to make another run this year, but has to replace some key parts. They are a younger team with Alex Karaban and Tarris Reed Jr. both moving on. Overall, they bring back five players, but one is Solo Ball, who is projected to miss the season after having surgery on his left wrist. Braylon Mullins is back, and he is the leading returning scorer, averaging 12 points per game last year. Silas Demary Jr. will also see his role increase after a good season last year. Meanwhile, Na'jai Hinest is expected to be the anchor in the front court, coming in from Seton Hall. Further, Nils Machowski should make some noise. He was a sharp-shooter from three at Wofford and will look to bring that skill to UConn. The Huskies open the season on Monday night against Gardner-Webb before dates with Michigan and Wagner.

Texas made a run to the Sweet 16 last year, and expectations are high for this campaign, but will it all come together for the Longhorns? They bring back Matas Vokietaitis, who averaged 15.6 points with 71 rebounds. They also bring in a ton of transfers. Isaiah Johnson comes in from Colorado, while David Punch comes in from TCU. They also added Mikey Lewis, Amari Evans, and Elyjah Freeman. Still, many of them are taking a step up in competition, going to the SEC. The freshman group is also solid, led by Bo Ogden and Austin Goosby. If they can make an impact, Texas can go far. They open the season against Chicago State before games with Gardner-Webb and Grambling.

John Calipari has brought the number one recruiting class in the nation to Arkansas. Jordan Smith Jr. and Abdou Toure both come into the program as five-stars. Smith was the third-ranked player in the nation, while Toure was 14th. Arkansas brought in four players ranked inside the top 20 overall, and also the top five at their position. Billy Richmond III returns after a solid sophomore campaign, and his minutes should increase this year. Meanwhile, Jeremiah Wilkinson comes in via the transfer portal. Calipari has always been good at getting the most out of a young roster and will need to do the same here. They open the season on Tuesday night against Arkansas Pine-Bluff before games against Virginia and Robert Morris.

Houston is coming off a down year by their standards. They went 30-7, most losses Kelvin Sampson and Houston have racked up since 2020. They also finished second in the Big 12, after winning the conference in back-to-back seasons. Still, it was a run to the Sweet 16, their seventh straight run that far. If Houston is going to make another run, Joseph Tugler will need to take another step forward. Houston did not have the interior presence they have had in years past, but Tugler showed signs of growth. Meanwhile, Dedan Thomas Jr. and Delreccor Gillespie are projected to play major roles this year, coming in as transfers. The Cougars open the season Monday night agaisnt La Salle, before dates with Cal and Jacksonville State.

Kansas opens the season ranked fairly low in the polls. They are 17th in the AP poll and 18th in the Coaches poll. Still, this team has national championship aspirations, and should have them. Tre White returns for his fifth year after shooting nearly 40 percent from three last year. Melvin Council Jr. also is back after a court ruling gave him eligibility. Still, the player to watch is Tyran Stokes Jr. He could be the national Freshman of the Year and the number one pick in the 2027 NBA Draft. The forward is a great scorer and facilitator. The faster he can make an impact, the better. Kansas opens up their campaign against Fordham on Monday, before dates with Middle Tennessee and Kentucky.

Tennessee is not likely to stay at this spot long. Rick Barnes has led the Volunteers to the Elite Eight three straight seasons, but returns just two players from last season. DeWayne Brown is back after a solid freshman season. He made just a handful of starts last year, and looks to take a step forward this year. Still, the Vols bring in a ton of solid players. Jalen Haralson comes in after a solid freshman campaign from Notre Dame. Juke Harris was a beast for Wake Forest last year, coming away with 21.4 points and 6.5 rebounds per game. Terrence Hill Jr. joins the squad from VCU after being the A-10 Tournament MVP. If this group can gel quickly, the team will be solid. If not, they could free fall in the rankings early. Their first test comes on Tuesday against Wofford, before games with Radford and Tennessee State.

Rick Pitino has resurrected St. John's. They had not won the Big East since the early 1990s under Lou Carnesecca, but have won it two years in a row. Now, they look for the three-peat. Quinn Ellis is the story for this team. The incoming point guard has spent recent years playing in Europe, primarily in Italy, at a professional level. Still, he was cleared to play by the NCAA. Meanwhile, Ian Jackson will be the primary scorer, returning for his junior season. Keyshawn Hall comes in from Auburn , and he will control the boards and be a solid secondary scoring threat. The Red Storm will contend in the conference once again, and open their season against Monmouth before fixtures against Iona and Colgate.

Alabama got dominated in the paint last year in their Sweet 16 exit. Nate Oats is trying to make sure that does not happen again. Drew Fielder arrives from Boise State and will give the Tide a presence down low. Brandon Harrison, once a starter at Oklahoma State, comes in from Kentucky, expecting to see an expanded role with the Tide. In their exhibition with Auburn, Alabama showed off some of their new physicality. Still, this will be a team based on a high-scoring, fast-paced offense. They bring back Aden Holloway and Amari Allen, who should play a major role in that offensive attack. If everything clicks in the paint, Alabama will be a very dangerous team. They open their season on Tuesday agaisnt Sam Houston before dates with Arkansas State and Oakland.

Louisville is coming in with an almost entirely new roster. Adrian Wolley is the sole returner from the rotation last year, but this team should still be solid. Jackson Shelstad, Karter Knox, and Seth Trimble all come in as transfer guards. Then there is Alvaro Folgueiras, who was the Horizon League Player of the Year as a Sophomore for Robert Morris and was solid last year for Iowa. He not only can play in the post, but also stretches out well to the three-point range. Former McDonald's All-American Flory Bidunga also joins the roster, coming in from Kansas . The big question is how they shift their style of play. This is a more defensive unit with size and athleticism against the heavy offensive focus of years past. Louisville opens their season Monday night against Chattanooga before dates with Morehead State and Memphis.

The defending national champions check in at 15. Mike Boynton slides over a spot on the bench, taking over for Dusty May. Michigan's ranking in the AP Poll is currently low, sitting 16th, but the team can turn that around quickly. Elliot Cadeau and Trey McKenney are back, but the team still needs to replace Morez Johnson Jr., Aday Mara, and Yaxel Lendeborg. Still, Roddy Gayle Jr. could be the difference in how well this team does. He was once a starter, but moved to a bench role last year, where he thrived. He is expected to be back in the starting lineup, and if he can continue that success with more minutes, Michigan will be in a good spot. Michigan opens up on Monday night against Oakland before games with UConn and Marquette.

The experience this group brings back is one ofthe best in the nation. They are expected to have JT Toppin at some point this year, as he works back from a torn ACL. Still, Donovan Atwell, Darrion Williams and Jamichael Stillwell are all part of the 2022 class that will have a fifth year of eligibility. The expected starting five has some of the most firepower in the nation, which will make Texas Tech a great team this year. The biggest worry is if somehow the trio of class of 2022 players lose their eligibility, or if Toppin does not return as expected. Until that happens, watch out for Texas Tech. They open up their season on Monday agaisnt Jackson State before clashes with Bethune-Cookman and Illinois.

No one has more returning production in the ACC than Virginia. They return eight players from last year, with over half of their points and minutes. Thijs De Ridder was named the ACC Preseason Player of the Year, while Sam Lewis is moving into a wing role this year. The Cavaliers also have Johann Grunloh, a massive rim defender and an anchor in the paint. Chance Mallory was a beast as a sixth man last year, and will be moving into the starting lineup. If he meets expectations, UVA could be a Top Ten team. They open the season against Drexel on Tuesday before facing Northeastern and Arkansas.

Malik Reneau is a star. Last year he averaged 18.9 points per game while snagging 6.5 rebounds. He is back this year for the Hurricanes and could be one of the best interior scoring threats in the nation. The Miami front court should be great this year, with Shelton Henderson and Somto Cyril. Caleb Gaskins looked good coming off the bench in camp and the exhibitions and could be a major part of this. The player to watch is Acaden Lewis, though. If he can help the Hurricanes develop an outside scoring threat, the sky is the limit for this team. Miami does not start out with an easy schedule. They will face off with Florida on Monday night before games agaisnt Wagner and North Florida.

UCLA is having a stellar year in football and could be set up for the same on the court. The team lost Tyler Bilodeau and Donovan Dent, while Eric Freeny is currently on a medical leave of absence. Still, they have some stars. Trent Perry is a preseason All-Big Ten player, while Eric Dailey Jr. is a massive scoring threat. The major wildcard will be Nikola Kusturica. He is only 17, but the 6-foot-9 player is physical and great on defense. If he can handle the physicality of the college basketball game, and specifically the Big Ten, he could change the offense as well. UCLA opens up the year on Monday night against Arizona before games with North Florida and Arkansas Pine-Bluff.

Iowa State is another team with a completely revamped lineup. Milan Momcilovic is at Kentucky while Joshua Jefferson is off to the NBA. Further, Killyan Toure is sidelined with a shoulder injury. He will be back for the stretch run of the season, which will be massive for the team. Meanwhile, Tamin Lipsey is back after a season averaging 12.5 points and 5.1 assists per game. Blake Buchanan will anchor the front court and will see an expanded role this year. The Cyclones open the regular season agaisnt Memphis on Monday before dates with Southern Miss and Southern.

USC is looking for a bounceback year and will be led by Rodney Rice. The senior is a former star, but is working back from injury. He played just six games last year, but averaged 20.3 points per game when on the court. Meanwhile, Alijah Arenas is a massive perimeter threat and primed for a breakout. They also bring in KJ Lewis and Eric Reibe through the transfer portal. Adonis and Darius Ratliff are two highly touted freshmen who could be a huge difference in the front court as well. USC opens up the season Monday night against Milwaukee, and also has upcoming games agaisnt Wichita State and Cal.

Vanderbilt expected Tyler Tanner to head to the NBA Draft, but he withdrew and is back at Vandy. Tanner is the scoring leader of this team after scoring 19.5 points per game last year. Meanwhile, Jackson Sheffield has looked great so far in his freshman year. They bring in plenty of transfers and have a much more physical roster. Bagot Dak comes in from Colorado while Berke Buyuktucel comes in from Nebraska. Both are massive physical presences which could change the shape of the Vandy roster. The Commodores open the season on Monday against Bellarmine, with games agaisnt Wake Forest and Memphis next on the slate.

Welcome to the PAC-12, Gonzaga. Under Mark Few, Gonzaga has dominated the WCC. Since he took over in 1999-00, they have never finished worse than second in the conference, made the tournament every year, and won both the regular season and conference tournament titles in the same year 19 times. Now they will look to repeat that success in a new conference. Gonzaga is the pick to win the league and bring back Braden Huff, who is an All-American candidate this year. Gonzaga opens their season against Purdue on Monday, with New Mexico State and LSU on the horizon.

Mark Pope is entering year three as the Kentucky head coach and brought in a haul in the transfer portal. Milan Momcilovic is the main man to watch. He was a stud for Iowa State and is one ofthe best shooters in the nation. The team also added Zoom Diallo, Franck Kepnand, Alex Wilkins, and Jerone Morton. Freshman Mason Williams also turned heads in the preseason, while sophomore Malachi Moreno will anchor the front court. He is a strong two-way player who will make an immediate impact. The Wildcats open the season Tuesday against Manhattan, and will play James Madison and Kansas early on.

If Robbie Avila is able to play, this is a completely different team. Like many players, he is looking for another year of eligibility, and it is currently up in the air if he will get it. Avila will miss the opener, but could get that extra season. He was the Atlantic 10 player of the Year last year, shooting 41 percent from three while also snagging 4.5 rebounds and adding 4.1 assists per game. Saint Louis won 29 games last year, and six of the top seven players are back on the team. They also added a top-20 freshman in Jamel Thomas and brought in some solid transfers. They open up the season on Monday against Lehigh before a date with Missouri.

articles.title: 😳 After disallowed goal: Bayern break BVB hearts
articles.summary: The first half of Der Klassiker was absolute chaos. After Olise rattled the woodwork with a spectacular effort just minutes in, the two teams went toe to toe...
articles.body:
The first half of Der Klassiker was absolute chaos. After Olise rattled the woodwork with a spectacular effort just minutes in, the two teams went toe to toe in a fierce battle, with BVB briefly looking to have taken the lead.

But only briefly: after Jobe Bellingham put the Black and Yellows 1-0 up, referee Tobias Stieler was called over to the VAR monitor.

And with good reason. Not only was Chukwuemeka offside when Bellingham shot, but he also clearly jumped into Urbig.

Bayern wasted no time in making them pay. Just two minutes after the disallowed goal, Olise played a superb through ball to Laimer, who put Bayern ahead with a true poacher's finish.

Der Klassiker is certainly living up to its billing so far.

articles.title: Falkirk v Celtic – Team News, Referee Details, Kick-Off Time & Where to Watch
articles.summary: Celtic will make the 29 miles trip to the Falkirk stadium tomorrow looking to collect the three points to open up a seven point advantage at the top of the S...
articles.body:
Celtic will make the 29 miles trip to the Falkirk stadium tomorrow looking to collect the three points to open up a seven point advantage at the top of the Scottish Premiership…

Mika Baur of Celtic is crowded out by Dundee United players Celtic v Dundee United, Scottish Premiership, Celtic Park, 28 October 2026. Mark Runnacles IMAGO Shutterstock

Despite plenty of troubles in European football, Celtic enter the second round of matches having lost one, draw one and won nine of the games, now having faced every side in the league.

Falkirk manager John McGlynn during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Falkirk at Celtic Park on August 29, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

John McGlynn's side started the season poorly but have found some significant form in recent weeks, picking up maximum points from their last three matches, most recently picking up all three points against Aberdeen at Pittodrie.

Celtic dropped two points against Dundee United in midweek, in a confused performance and team selection which resulted in the Celtic captain Callum McGregor observing that Celtic needs to stop playing 'basketball'.

Auston Trusty is unavailable as he is back home in the States attending a celebration of his late father's life with his family. Alistair Johnston is sidelined with a hamstring injury and while Joel van den Berg is back on the grass with the first team squad, this match will be too early for him. Yang remains sidelined for a week or two longer after his injury picked up at the recent Asian Cup.

Martin O'Neill is currently giving Sam Johnstone a run of first team games before deciding if the former England goalkeeper will be his first pick keeper for the rest of the season ahead of Viljami Sinisalo.

25th October 2026; Easter Road; Scottish Premiership Football, Hibernian versus Celtic; Cameron Carter Vickers of Celtic. Photo Vagelis Georgariou

Cameron Carter-Vickers is fit and available and as Celtic's best central defender really should be including in the starting eleven. Ange Postecoglou and Brendan Rodgers would have had fit CCV as a first name on the teamsheet, so hopefully Martin does the same tomorrow.

With Trusty unavailable, Liam Scales will start at the left hand side of Celtic central defence with Colby Donovan at right back and Kieran Tierney at left back.

Callum McGregor of Celtic and Bert Esselink of Dundee United Celtic v Dundee United, Scottish Premiership, Celtic Park, 28 October 2026. Photo Mark Runnacles IMAGO Shutterstock

What can be done about Celtic's middle three? Mika Baur must start and it's hard to imagine Callum McGregor dropping to the bench, unless his midweek comments have ruffled feathers. The manager though said he agreed with what the captain said, so he starts. Maybe it's worth dropping Benjamin Nygren to the bench and bringing Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain into the side? He certain merits a start and is being wasted as an unused sub, or getting the last quarter of an hour occasionally.

25th October 2026; Easter Road; Scottish Premiership Football, Hibernian versus Celtic; Kasper Hogh of Celtic. Photo Vagelis Georgariou

Muddled thinking in midweek saw Kasper Hogh play centre forward but with no wingers then when the wingers arrived he departed the scene will his scoring drought extended. Play Hogh through the middle and have Haissem Hassan on the right wing. On the left wing it would be tempting to start Jota but taking into account the artificial surface and his injury issues, it might be best for him to sit this one out. Camilo Duran could be asked to play wide left, and he'll still be looking for a goal.

Colby Donovan of Celtic controls the ball during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Hearts at Celtic Park on October 18, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Johnstone; Donovan, Carter-Vickers, Scales, Tierney; McGregor, Baur, Oxlade Chamberlain; Hassan, Hogh and Duran.

Subs: Sinisalo, Jota, Emenalo, Sorensen, Murray, Nygren, Osmand, Mheuka, Forrest.

articles.title: Who is Blake Barnett? What to know about Kansas State's latest QB
articles.summary: Kansas State made a switch at quarterback during the first quarter of its game at Colorado. Blake Barnett is in the game.
articles.body:
BOULDER, Co. — Blake Barnett, come on down.

Barnett came off the bench for Kansas State in the first quarter of its Oct. 31 game at Colorado , after sophomore Dillon Duff started at quarterback .

Duff's first three drives resulted in three-and-outs. The Wildcats gained 16 total yards, and Duff took a pair of sacks .

Barnett is the fourth quarterback to take meaningful snaps in the last three weeks. Avery Johnson and Jacob Knuth were ruled out ahead of the Big 12 matchup.

See our best photos from Kansas State football at Arizona State in Week 8

Blake Barnett missed a lot of time due to injury

It will be worth monitoring Barnett's health throughout the game. He's been on crutches for most of the season and only recently came off the injury report.

Barnett was the first quarterback off the bench in the Wildcats' Week 1 blowout against Nicholls, relieving Johnson after he built a comfortable lead. He completed 4 of 5 passes for 41 yards.

After that, Barnett was on crutches. He was a game-time decision heading into last week's game at Arizona State when Knuth got the start.

Blake Barnett was used as a power-runner last season

Barnett played in four games last season and was used in special packages as a running quarterback. A bigger 6-foot-1, 218-pound frame, Barnett was a change-of-pace power runner K-State could use when it had other healthy quarterbacks.

Barnett rushed 14 times for 40 yards last year and didn't throw a pass.

Blake Barnett played high school football in Colorado

Making his first career start against the Buffaloes is only fitting for a quarterback who shined at Erie High School in Colorado, which is about 16 miles down the road from Folsom Field.

Barnett was Colorado's top-ranked 2024 player, and Rivals rated him as the seventh-best dual-threat QB in the entire class.

Barnett led Erie to a 36-7 record during his career, including a state championship as a senior. He broke the Colorado state record for overall touchdowns with 159, which was previously owned by some guy named Christian McCaffrey.

He threw for 7,518 yards and 88 touchdowns and ran for 3,420 yards and 68 scores during his career.

articles.title: Who is Arafat Minhas, Pakistan cricket’s rising star all-rounder?
articles.summary: A calm head on young shoulders, Arafat Minhas has swiftly earned the reputation of a match-winner for Pakistan.
articles.body:
At five wickets down with 125 required off 79 balls, Pakistan were teetering on the edge of yet another batting collapse when Arafat Minhas walked in to bat in the final of the One-Day International (ODI) tri-nation cricket series against Sri Lanka.

An expectant home crowd in Lahore was on tenterhooks as the 21-year-old all-rounder began his batting partnership with Hasan Nawaz under the floodlights of the Gaddafi Stadium on Saturday.

Minhas, who had gone wicketless in Sri Lanka’s innings, showed few signs of the pressure mounting on the young batting pair and began the repair job.

Within a few overs, the run chase swayed back in Pakistan’s favour but the final remained tense.

With the hosts needing 39 runs from 27 balls, Sri Lanka’s Dasun Shanaka bowled a delivery at length, angling the ball into Minhas.

Unnerved by the occasion and his own lack of experience, the batter swung his bat across the line and sent the ball soaring over midwicket for six to ignite the crowd and rekindle lost hope.

Following this defining moment of his innings, Arafat coolly went on to hit four more sixes, finish with 61 runs off 31 balls, help Pakistan clinch the trophy and bag himself the player of the series award.

He ended the series with nine wickets and 149 runs, including two half-centuries.

Commentators on the host broadcast ran out of superlatives for the promising all-rounder, who admitted that he “enjoyed the pressure” of the final run-chase and tried to remain calm.

“The team needed someone to believe that we could achieve the target.”

Before shining with the bat in the final, Arafat produced one of the finest bowling performances of his fledgling international career against England in Rawalpindi on October 10.

After scoring 59 off 58 balls to help Pakistan recover from 81-4 and post 302-9, Minhas took six wickets for 40 runs as England were bowled out for 215, handing Pakistan an 87-run win.

England were at 91 without losing a wicket before Arafat dismantled their batting order.

Among his victims was swashbuckling batter Harry Brook, who was bowled for five by a delivery that turned past his attempted defensive shot and hit the stumps.

The England captain was left stunned at the crease and in the post-match media talk.

“Is he under 21? I didn’t know,” Brook said after the match.

More plaudits poured in as Minhas showed his all-round skills on the field.

“A half-century, six wickets and a run out. Mike Hesson wants all-round cricketers and he’s found one in Arafat Minhas,” former England captain Nasser Hussain said during the broadcast.

The performance made him the third Pakistani to score a half-century and take at least five wickets in a men’s ODI after Shahid Afridi and Abdul Razzaq.

On his ODI debut against Australia in May, Arafat took 5-32, becoming the first Pakistani to claim a five-wicket haul on debut, as well as winning the player of the series award.

“I prefer not to label players as batting or bowling all-rounders,” Minhas later said in an interview with the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB). “I’d rather be seen as a complete all-rounder.”

Thirteen years earlier, Minhas dreamed of becoming a fast bowler like every other aspiring Pakistani cricketer.

But the then-eight-year-old was handed a leather cricket ball and instructed to take up left-arm spin by his father, Kashif, who spent years helping Arafat develop the all-round skills that are now helping Pakistan win matches.

Kashif had represented his hometown team, Multan, in under-19 cricket but was forced to give up on his dream – “with a heavy heart” – by his father, who urged him to take over the family’s car showroom business.

Years later, watching his sons play with toy eggs and plastic balls, Kashif saw a spark.

“When I observed them, I saw their playing style wasn’t ordinary; it seemed like a natural gift and a blessing from God,” Kashif told Al Jazeera. “I thought: ‘why not train them for professional cricket’?”

He would go on to buy full kits for his sons, setting them on the path towards professional cricket.

“My father handed me a hard ball when I was about eight or nine and I’ve bowled left-arm spin ever since [but] In tape-ball cricket, I used to bowl fast,” Minhas explained when asked about his control on his bowling variations.

Minhas rapidly progressed through Pakistan’s age-group system, becoming the country’s best under-16 player in his final year before breaking into the under-19 team.

In 2020, when the COVID-19 pandemic lockdown threatened to interrupt his sons’ development, Kashif built a cricket practice facility on the rooftop of his house in Multan.

A net, a mat pitch and floodlights were installed to ensure that “practice wouldn’t stop”.

In 2024, when Pakistan reached the semifinals of the ICC Under-19 World Cup and lost to Australia by one wicket, Minhas played a key role in the team’s progress in the tournament.

Given his standout performances, the young all-rounder’s elevation to the senior team seemed inevitable.

Minhas’s younger brother, Sameer, is a prodigious right-handed opening batter who has also made significant progress.

Last week, he was included in Pakistan’s Test squad for the two-match series against Sri Lanka in November.

Playing his first season of first-class cricket, Sameer scored 405 runs in seven matches, following his own promising spell with Pakistan’s under-19 team. Their youngest brother, Abdullah, is also pursuing cricket as a left-handed batter and leg-spinner.

“To move forward, I’ll improve and put in whatever extra work is required,” Minhas said after the England match. “This isn’t the final goal. The ultimate goal is much further ahead.”

Kashif’s ambition extends beyond one son’s career. He wishes for all three boys to play together for Pakistan and win an international trophy – a dream that would give a new ending to the cricketing journey he had to abandon.

“My ultimate dream is to see all three of my sons play together in the Pakistan playing XI and bring home an ICC trophy for Pakistan. That’s the day my dream will be complete, and that void will truly be filled.”

articles.title: 6 Potential NHL Landing Spots for Nikita Kucherov After Reported Trade Request
articles.summary: We're used to trade drama at this point in an already wild NHL season, but the biggest bombshell yet dropped Friday: Nikita Kucherov informed the Lightning that he will not re-sign and would like to be traded.
articles.body:
We're used to trade drama at this point in an already wild NHL season, but the biggest bombshell yet dropped Friday: Nikita Kucherov informed the Lightning that he will not re-sign and would like to be traded.

Later that night, Lightning GM Julien BriseBois said the club has "no intention of trading Nikita."

Kucherov is a pending unrestricted free agent, and the two sides clearly haven't been able to come to an agreement on an extension. While it seems likely he will continue to play for the Lightning for at least a while, he could eventually go the Dylan Larkin route and force Tampa Bay's hand by sitting out games. If so, here are six potential landing spots for the 33-year-old reigning Hart Trophy winner.

The defending champion Hurricanes, who have started this year looking like a back-to-back Cup win is imminent, would be an enticing landing spot for any player, especially a star at the tail end of his prime like Kucherov.

The Hurricanes currently have $8,010,259 in cap space , according to Puckpedia, and four first-round picks over the next three years. They could relatively easily fit the last season of Kucherov's $9.5 million cap hit onto their roster, and they've got some enticing draft capital that the Lightning could use. Plus, they've got an unhappy camper looking for a change of scenery in young defenseman Alex Nikishin to offer, who signed a one-year deal for $3 million but was reportedly looking to play elsewhere during the offseason .

The questions become: What is Kucherov really looking for here? Would the Hurricanes invest in him long-term, or would both sides be fine with a rental situation? And of course, are the Lightning willing to give an in-conference contender a Hart Trophy winner?

It's a win-now year for the Wild if there ever has been one. They're first in the Central and gaining steam with a 9-3-3 record and a goal differential of 12, and they're still hanging onto pending unrestricted free agent Quinn Hughes -- for now. Many think they're trying to acquire friend of Hughes and trade requestor Dylan Larkin, but could Kucherov's sudden availability change things?

Minnesota's biggest need is still a center, but Kucherov is Kucherov . Plus, he's got arguably better playmaking ability than any other winger and plenty of premier centers in the NHL. The Kucherov-Kirill Kaprizov connection could be pure magic.

It all comes down to what Tampa Bay is looking for, which is completely unknown at this point. The Wild have all their future first-round picks, but their prospect pool is wearing thin after going all-in on Hughes.

The Habs followed up their exciting playoff run with a shaky start to the season, but they appear to have stabilized on this four-game win streak. They're sitting at second in the Atlantic now with a 8-3-2 record and a goal-differential of five.

Kucherov could really keep the momentum going and give this team even more high-end skill and a bit more veteran experience. Montreal could use one more true star player to round out its top two lines.

Now, an in-division trade between two potential playoff teams involving a Hart Trophy winner seems pretty unlikely. The return would have to be gigantic, but at the same time, this feels like the best fit for Kucherov. The Canadiens have done a great job locking down their young core at reasonable prices, and they've got nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season to sign Kucherov to an extension.

Also, Kucherov's former teammate Martin St. Louis is Montreal's head coach. You have to think as much as the Lightning might be deterred to do this, it really does make the most sense of all the options.

It's no secret that the Rangers are struggling without Igor Shesterkin, and that a season that started with such promise is more than likely now a wash. But let's think about what Kucherov is actually seeking in a landing spot.

If winning were the main driver, he wouldn't have requested a trade from the Lightning. Tampa is in a playoff spot, and they're 7-2-1 in their last 10 games.

The Rangers have the cap space to fit the last season of his current contract in without Shesterkin, and they are looking at about $38 million in cap space to fill out the roster next season. They've got to extend Gabe Perreault, Will Cuylle, and a few others, but they could realistically give Kucherov upwards of $20 million , according to The Athletic's Chris Johnston, who says he is reportedly seeking that. They could also give him the opportunity to play with countrymen like Vladislav Gavrikov, Pavel Dorofeyev, and the now-injured Igor Shesterkin for the long term.

The problem is, the Rangers aren't necessarily just a Kucherov away from contending. They'd have to make sure they could immediately sign him to an extension; otherwise, the risk of losing him after a rental season makes absolutely no sense.

If the Lightning want to avoid sending Kucherov to a contender, you could see them signing off on this one. If the Rangers sent over Perreault, they'd have even more space to make a Kucherov extension work, and it would be extremely difficult for the Lightning to turn a player of that caliber with that much potential down.

Kucherov r eportedly wants to play alongside a star , according to ESPN's Emily Kaplan. Can you imagine how electric the Macklin Celebrini-to-Kucherov connection would be? That alone forces you to consider a deal between the Lightning and the Sharks.

The Sharks are still a few years away from Cup contention, so they'd have to bank on Kucherov's longevity, as he's not getting any younger at 33 years old. The Sharks are struggling at even strength, though, and a player like Kucherov specifically could come in and turn that around.

They've got an abundance of superb young players to toss at the Lightning, but how much do they really want to mess with their rebuild and chemistry, and how much is the Lightning going to ask for?

The timeline isn't perfect here, but the Sharks have the cap space and the superstar Kucherov is apparently seeking. If the player holds the most leverage in the situation, you get the sense he'd wind up in San Jose. But the two teams in question do have to sign off on this, after all. We'll see how much GM Mike Grier is willing to part ways with.

The Mammoth have not shied away from going after big-name players, even if they don't always win the sweepstakes. They were in on Connor Hellebuyck, and it seems like they've expressed interest in Dylan Larkin.

This is a team that is about two players away from longer playoff runs and perennial contention. Not to mention, they've got no major pending free agents with their young core locked up, and they're projected to have just over $25 million in salary cap space next season, according to Puckpedia.

Kucherov would work great alongside a budding star like Logan Cooley. While the Mammoth should really focus on fixing their goaltending situation, a player like Kucherov could only help in the meantime.

Again, the possibility of this deal depends on what Tampa Bay is looking for in return. If the Lightning are focusing on futures and prospects, they might be inclined to do business with the Mammoth. If they're looking to go the established player route, it's harder to imagine Kucherov in Utah.

articles.title: Nikita Kucherov 'Committed' to Lightning After Trade Request, Jon Cooper Says
articles.summary: Tampa Bay Lightning head coach Jon Cooper says he's confident Nikita Kucherov "wants to be a part of this team for this season" despite his trade request, per Eduardo A. Encina of the Tampa Bay Times.
articles.body:
Tampa Bay Lightning head coach Jon Cooper says he's confident Nikita Kucherov "wants to be a part of this team for this season" despite his trade request, per Eduardo A. Encina of the Tampa Bay Times.

"He is committed to be with the group that loves him and the group he loves," Cooper said ahead of the Lightning's Saturday road game against the Nashville Predators, per Encina.

Cooper added he expects nothing to change either in his coaching of Kucherov's play going forward, per Encina.

"Jon Cooper will coach the team the way Jon Cooper has always coached the team and Kuch is going to play like the superstar he is and the way he has for a decade and a half and that is how it is going to continue," Cooper said, per Encina. "All the rest of it is outside noise and, for Kuch internally, what happens after our season is over, that's Kuch's right and he has earned that right for whatever happens.

"For us, it's probably made the team stronger."

Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported Friday Kucherov had requested a trade after telling the Lightning he would not re-sign with the team this offseason.

General manager Julien BriseBois responded with a statement in which he said the Lightning "unequivocally have no intention of trading Nikita."

Kucherov's agent Dan Milstein confirmed Saturday his client would continue playing for the Lightning despite his trade request, per TSN's Pierre LeBrun .

"Of course. He loves playing hockey," Milstein said about whether Kucherov would continue playing, per LeBrun. "He will play while I will take care of the business side going forward."

The news comes after Connor Hellebuyck refused to attend Winnipeg Jets training camp and Dylan Larkin sat out regular-season action with the Detroit Red Wings following their own trade requests earlier this year.

Kucherov told his teammates about his trade request during their Friday flight to Nashville, according to LeBrun.

He started out his first game since the request by assisting on each of the Lightning's first three goals against the Predators.

Kucherov is playing this season on an expiring contract with a $9.5 million cap hit. He can authorize trades to 10 teams as part of the deal, per PuckPedia .

ESPN's Emily Kaplan reported "Kucherov has his eyes set on playing with another one of the league's top superstars and has a few players/teams in mind."

The Lightning drafted Kucherov in 2013 shortly after the organization hired Cooper as head coach.

Kucherov developed into one of the NHL's top forwards before leading the franchise to consecutive Stanley Cups in 2020 and 2021. He has claimed three Art Ross Trophies and two Hart Trophies as a member of the franchise.

The winger earned his most recent MVP honor after leading the Lightning to a ninth straight playoff berth with 130 points in 76 games last season.

Kucherov, who has 15 points (four goals, 11 assists) in his first 12 games of the season, passed Steven Stamkos as the Lightning's all-time points leader less than a week prior to his trade request.

Stamkos, another core member of the Lightning's back-to-back Cup runs, departed Tampa Bay when he signed with the Predators ahead of the 2024-25 campaign.

The Lightning are heading into Saturday in fourth place in the Atlantic after an 8-3-1 start to the season. It sounds like as of now BriseBois and Cooper intend to push for a final playoff run with Kucherov this spring, even if it comes at the cost of the winger following Stamkos' lead by leaving in free agency this offseason.

articles.summary: ¿Nuevo colombiano a la Premier League? El equipo inglés que busca a Carlos Andrés Gómez
articles.body: El extremo colombiano Carlos Andrés Gómez podría dar el salto a la Premier League de Inglaterra. Tras un año de gran consolidación en el fútbol brasileño vistiendo los colores de Vasco da Gama, sus actuaciones en Sudamérica y en la Selección Colombia han vuelto a despertar el interés de varios clubes de primera línea en Europa. El conjunto inglés Bournemouth sigue muy de cerca los pasos del atacante de 24 años y ya habría iniciado conversaciones preliminares para explorar su fichaje de cara a la ventana de transferencias de enero. Según reportes del periodista especializado en mercado Ekrem Konur, la directiva y el cuerpo técnico de las Cheries valoran enormemente la versatilidad, velocidad y potencia en el uno contra uno de Gómez, pudiendo desempeñarse sin problemas por ambas bandas en el ataque. Además, en la directiva del club inglés consideran un factor determinante su paso previo por el Rennes de Francia (Ligue 1), un recorrido en el balompié europeo que facilitaría su rápida adaptación al ritmo físico y táctico del fútbol británico. De concretarse la operación, Gómez se sumaría a la lista de futbolistas colombianos que han pasado por la disciplina del Bournemouth, camino que abrieron previamente Jefferson Lerma y Luis Sinisterra. Su brillante campaña en la Serie A brasileña no solo lo devolvió a la órbita europea, sino que lo consolidó dentro de las convocatorias de la Selección Colombia. Aunque el Bayer Leverkusen alemán también ha monitoreado la situación del jugador, el Bournemouth figura como el club más activo en las gestiones iniciales. Las próximas semanas serán clave para conocer si la escuadra de la Premier League concreta una oferta formal ante la directiva del Vasco da Gama.

articles.title: USA Sports and NBC claim record WNBA Finals ratings, but the comparisons leave out important context
articles.summary: WNBA Finals TV ratings claims face scrutiny as USA Sports combines streaming and TV numbers without clear breakdowns or independent verification.
articles.body: USA Sports announced Saturday that Game 6 of the WNBA Finals averaged 1.5 million viewers on Thursday afternoon. I'll admit, that number raised my eyebrows. A game that tipped off at 12:30 p.m. Eastern, or 9:30 a.m. in the morning in the Golden State Valkyries' home market, outdrew last year's championship clincher in primetime? USA Sports says it did, by 4%. The release combines viewers across USA Network, E! and SYFY with streaming led by Peacock, but doesn't break out how much of the audience came from television or streaming. WNBA BAILED OUT OF SCHEDULING DISASTER AS ANGEL REESE, DREAM FORCE GAME 7 USA Sports and NBC Sports have been promoting record audiences throughout the Finals, with WNBA PR also distributing their releases through an NBA employee. NBC called its 2.1 million audience for Game 1 the largest ever for a Finals opener. USA Sports touted Game 3's 1.71 million as the biggest Game 3 audience since 1999 and the highest ever on cable. Those figures, like the Game 6 announcement, combined television and streaming. NBC's television audience didn't top the old ESPN record NBC called Game 4 between the Valkyries and Atlanta Dream the most-watched Game 4 in WNBA Finals history, reporting 1.9 million viewers across NBC and Peacock. The release touted a 14% increase over the previous record of 1.67 million for the New York Liberty and Minnesota Lynx on ESPN in 2024. Keep in mind, ESPN requires paid access. NBC is available free over the air, and this year's game also had Peacock. According to Sports Media Watch, NBC's television audience was 1.66 million, slightly below the previous reported ESPN record. Another 232,000 came from streaming measured separately by Adobe Analytics. That addition put NBC's combined figure over the old mark, but NBC didn't include the breakdown in its release. DREAM, VALKYRIES LEAVE COURT BEFORE T.I.'S 10-YEAR-OLD DAUGHTER SINGS WNBA FINALS ANTHEM I wrote about this measurement issue in July, when CBS and NBC both claimed the season's biggest WNBA audience. Even the Nielsen numbers come from different measurement systems. Nielsen made Big Data + Panel its standard in 2025, combining its household panel with information from smart TVs and set-top boxes across 45 million households. The 2024 ESPN figure predates that standard. Nielsen also expanded its out-of-home measurement in 2025, increasing coverage from 66% to 100% of the contiguous U.S. television population, and it includes viewing in places such as bars and restaurants. Then, on Aug. 31 of this year, it introduced changes intended to better capture how many people watch together, using wearable devices that pick up television audio. Nielsen says its changes are intended to improve accuracy and don't guarantee higher ratings. But if better measurement captures someone who was already watching the WNBA, that person isn't a new fan. Game 5's headline left out the size of the gap USA Sports promoted Monday's 1.4 million viewers across USA Network, CNBC and Peacock as the second-most-watched Finals Game 5 ever. Its release acknowledged that the 2024 Liberty-Lynx clincher held the record. What it didn't include was that game's audience: 2.15 million on ESPN, putting this year's reported total about 35% below it. The 2024 Finals were a best-of-five series, making Game 5 a winner-take-all matchup for the championship. The WNBA expanded to best-of-seven in 2025, and this year's Game 5 began with the series tied 2-2, so neither team could clinch the title. Monday's game also faced Cowboys-Eagles on "Monday Night Football," which drew 18.8 million viewers, plus the World Series at 8.3 million and NBA regular-season games. VALKYRIES PLAYER'S DAD PUTS WNBA ON BLAST FOR UNUSUAL FINALS START: 'LEAGUE'S FAULT' The release did, however, highlight an 8% increase over Game 2. It also described Game 5 as the "third consecutive game that USA Sports has posted record viewership." Who's checking the streaming numbers? The releases cite Adobe Analytics for their streaming audiences, but they don't identify who independently verified those figures or provide the data behind them. Adobe's documentation describes an average-minute audience calculation based on time spent watching divided by the content's duration or a selected reporting period. Its software lets customers choose reporting windows and, for certain calculations, whether viewing time includes commercials. NBC's release doesn't specify those settings or explain how the streaming calculation was matched to its television measurement. Michael Mulvihill, Fox's president of insights and analytics, posted on X that Nielsen had told clients: "Mixing internal or third-party data with Nielsen metrics to make comparative statements in the press is not permissible." He added, "Hopefully this clear, fair policy will be rigorously enforced during football season." NBC's own Sept. 14 release for the NFL season opener attributed its combined NBC and Peacock audience to "Nielsen Big Data inclusive of first party data." Its WNBA releases still combine Nielsen and Adobe figures. NBC should explain what independent verification applies to the WNBA streaming numbers and how its record claims fit Nielsen's policy. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD USA Sports changed the Nielsen source for Game 6 For Game 6, USA Sports cited Nielsen's "panel-only" data alongside Adobe Analytics. Its releases for Games 2, 3 and 5 used Nielsen's Big Data + Panel figures, plus Adobe. Nielsen says Big Data + Panel figures generally take two to three days to arrive, and its press policy allows preliminary reporting for single-day events. So, the panel-only figure could be an early estimate while USA Sports waits for the final number. The Game 6 release doesn't say that, though. And it doesn't label the figure preliminary or explain the switch. Game 6 was moved from 8 p.m. to 12:30 p.m. so it could be played at State Farm Arena, with the Hawks playing there that night. In announcing the move, the WNBA and NBA said they would join the broadcasters in a coordinated promotional push to get viewers to the new time slot. The move also took the game out of direct competition with "Thursday Night Football." USA Sports has enough confidence in the figure to rank Game 6 as the fifth-most-watched WNBA Finals game on cable. Then it should be able to tell us whether the number is final and how much of it actually came from cable.

articles.title: Transfer portal, not NIL, reason for parity, claims college football expert Brooks Austin
articles.summary: Brooks Austin argues the transfer portal, not NIL, drives college football parity as programs like Georgia and Alabama can no longer stockpile depth.
articles.body: It's no secret that college football has seen its fair share of parity over the past few years. A sport that was once dominated by the SEC, more specifically Alabama, has become completely wide open in terms of legitimate championship contenders. It all culminated in a team like Indiana, one of the worst programs in college football history, completing a 16-0 dream season with a national championship just last year. SEC'S CRAZY, HISTORY-MAKING WEEK 7 WEEKEND IS THE LATEST EXAMPLE OF COLLEGE FOOTBALL'S NEW ERA Now in 2026, the parity has reached an all-time high, with no truly dominant team standing out eight weeks into the season. Many fans and pundits alike have attributed this to the advent of NIL, and their reasoning is fairly sound. Of course, the proliferation of talent would become "flatter" when every program is allowed to legally pay money for players. Not everyone is on board with this theory, though, and one of the voices leading the charge in the opposite direction is none other than "The Film Guy," Brooks Austin. In an exclusive interview with OutKick, Austin reasoned that it's actually the transfer portal, and not NIL, that is the cause for all this chaos in the ranks of CFB. "Everybody blames it on NIL," he explains. "I think it has far more to do with freedom of movement. The portal has changed this more than anything else." As Austin puts it, teams like Bama and Georgia can no longer stack talent and stick it on the proverbial shelf for three years. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "Georgia can pay their backup just as much as Wake Forest can pay him to be a starter... so when a backup defensive tackle has been sitting on the bench for 2 years, he wants to play." Money is a factor, according to Austin, but it has just as much to do with the disappearance of depth as it does with overall funding. "I think NIL has certainly created some of this parity and created opportunities for dispersion of talent," he says. "But I think a lot of it also has to do with the fact that we're actually able to transfer, we're able to go." A perfect example is when the aforementioned Bulldogs and Crimson Tide met in the 2025 SEC Championship Game. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I remember last year in the SEC championship game, Georgia's down several starters on the offensive line, and Alabama is down several starters on their defensive line," Austin recalls. "I remember that same situation happening in 2022 before the portal got absolutely rampant and Georgia loses the starting left tackle and it's like, OK, don't worry. Here's Broderick Jones. He's a former five-star and he hasn't been playing at all, he's gonna go block Will Anderson for four quarters." "And, you know, Broderick. I don't know if he stays around for 2 years to sit on the bench nowadays, right?" A combination of NIL and the transfer portal is certainly proving to be the great equalizer in college football, but it's fairly clear one has a lot more to do with it than the other.

articles.title: WWE NXT Halloween Havoc 2026 Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights
articles.summary: Welcome to Bleacher Report's coverage of WWE NXT Halloween Havoc 2026.
articles.body:
Welcome to Bleacher Report's coverage of WWE NXT Halloween Havoc 2026.

Danhausen hosted this year's show, and several titles were on the line. Here is a look at the card from Saturday's event:

Wren Sinclair vs. Kelani Jordan (NXT Women's Championship)

Grayson Waller vs. Tony D'Angelo (NXT Championship)

Let's take a look at what went down at this year's Halloween Havoc.

The annual Halloween Havoc event actually took place on Halloween night this year instead of just happening on a day near the holiday, so WWE really leaned into it by having lots of people dressing in costumes. The fans in the crowd were embracing the spooky vibes, too.

Danhausen might not have had the best time hosting SmackDown thanks to Gunther attacking him, but he was hoping Halloween Havoc would give him a second chance.

He and the Minihausens came out to kick off the show with a promo in the ring. He hyped the show in his usual style, and he promised the NXT stars a night to remember because he turned several places in the arena into scare rooms.

The first bout was a Weapons Wild match, and it featured two men who used to be the best of friends. Tavion Heights took on his former tag team partner, Myles Borne.

Both men were dressed in special gear for the Halloween event. Heights took control initially, but Borne used a kendo stick to gain the advantage. His heel turn has had a slow start, but he has a look of intensity in his eyes that said he is ready to embrace his dark side.

The crowd popped when Heights grabbed a table from under the ring to set up at ringside, but Borne used a steel chair to cut him off before he could do anything with it.

These are two young, hungry wrestlers who have been impressive during their respective NXT runs, so seeing them get the spotlight at the beginning of the show was great. They clearly wanted to deliver a memorable performance, and they did not hold back with the physicality.

With WWE being the product that it is, this was never going to be a bloody mess, but they still found ways to make it feel violent without needing to rely on blading or using many weapons outside of the usual wrestling arsenal.

This was a strong performance from two guys who are still looking to make the jump into NXT's main event scene. Borne used one of the cameras to knock Heights off the top rope and through a table, allowing him to hit his finisher for the win.

Being sprayed with a fire extinguisher is not a fun experience. If anyone questions why it works in matches, it's because it would actually work in a fight.

It still feels weird to have commercial breaks during a a PLE. It just feels like an ordinary TV show.

The suplex onto the chair at ringside looked very painful.

Borne took a nasty shot from the trash can to the face like a champ.

The way Borne tried to pin Heights with a chair and the steel steps was creative.

articles.title: Injury update delivers huge blow to Patriots offense in Week 8
articles.summary: The Patriots will be missing two of their top skill weapons this week.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots will travel south to Hard Rock Stadium this week for an AFC East showdown with the Miami Dolphins , riding the momentum of their first win this season. The franchise's most recent injury update delivered a significant blow to its offensive firepower heading into the matchup.

The Patriots announced on Saturday that they will be without two star skill players this week: running back TreVeyon Henderson will miss the game due to illness, and wide receiver A.J. Brown will miss the game due to an ankle/knee injury.

Brown was one of the franchise's biggest offseason acquisitions and was intended to be a top target for Drake Maye. However, he suffered a high ankle sprain in the season opener against Seattle and was sidelined until Week 6. He has played in the team's past two games and has 101 receiving yards this season, but has been targeted heavily since his return.

Henderson has served as the team's No. 2 running back and has been efficient in his limited role this season. He has 203 rushing yards and one touchdown on 52 carries so far this year, along with five receptions for 45 yards.

articles.title: Grading Auburn in its loss to Ole Miss
articles.summary: Oct. 31—Assessing the Auburn Tigers for the totality of their collapse Saturday against the Ole Miss Rebels: Offense — F: A decent first half devolved into a...
articles.body:
Oct. 31—Assessing the Auburn Tigers for the totality of their collapse Saturday against the Ole Miss Rebels:

Offense — F: A decent first half devolved into a second-half ship wreck for the Tigers in Saturday's 45-15 loss. Auburn had 171 yards before halftime and 236 through three quarters. The fourth quarter should carry a parental advisory for the utter domination unleashed by the Rebels.

Defense — D: Trinidad Chambliss, if you haven't heard, is pretty good. By the end, Saturday was a walk in the park for the Rebels, who finished with 487 yards offense. They had 186 at halftime.

Special teams — D: Hunter Kaak averaged 43 yards on his four kicks, and Alex McPherson hit his only field-goal attempt, a 29-yarder at the end of the second quarter, but the Tigers suffered a blocked extra point. No returns recorded.

Coaching — G: Not good enough for an F. Going for two once they got within two in the third quarter, OK. Still going for two after a penalty, with over 21 minutes of game time remaining, highly questionable. That turned the momentum in a decisive manner, and the Rebels rolled off the final 28 points.

Overall — F: Again, have you heard: Auburn beat Georgia a few weeks back. That's about all the Tigers can hang their hat on ... for now. The kid shown late in the fourth quarter, an Ole Miss fan, brandishing a belt in an aggressive manner definitely symbolized what Ole Miss did at the end.

articles.title: No. 14 Wake Forest stretches its winning streak to five games with a 51-7 rout of Virginia
articles.summary: (AP) — Ty Clark III scored on three short runs, Gio Lopez threw a touchdown pass and Connor Calvert kicked three field goals Saturday as No. 14 Wake Forest p...
articles.body:
WINSTON-SALEM, N.C. (AP) — Ty Clark III scored on three short runs, Gio Lopez threw a touchdown pass and Connor Calvert kicked three field goals Saturday as No. 14 Wake Forest posted a 51-7 runaway win over Virginia to stretch its winning streak to five.

Wake Forest (7-1, 4-1 ACC) posted the second biggest margin of victory over the Cavaliers (4-5, 2-4 ACC) in the 54-game history of the series. In their last four games, the Demon Deacons have surrendered four touchdowns while scoring 187 points.

The Cavaliers have lost their last three. They faced the prospect of their first shutout since Virginia Tech took a 10-0 victory in 2017 before quarterback Beau Pribula connected with De'Shawn Martin on a 47-yard scoring play with 50 seconds left in the third quarter.

Lopez, who was 13 of 21 for 229 yards, suffered an apparent leg injury late in the third quarter, but was able to limp off the field. Steele Pizzella replaced Lopez and finished a scoring drive with Jamar Searcy's 7-yard scoring run.

Kyndall McCaleb chipped in a 27-yard touchdown run for Wake Forest in the fourth quarter.

Virginia entered Wake Forest territory twice in the first half, and each time, the Cavaliers met with disaster. Pribula threw a third-down interception from the Wake Forest 47, which the Demon Deacons converted into a 45-yard field goal from Calvert with 2:30 left in the first quarter.

The second trip may have been the most painful. The Cavaliers drove from their own 19 to the Wake Forest 6, but on a fourth-and-1, Zay Davis took the direct snap for no gain. The Demon Deacons cashed in that stand and got a 25-yard field goal from Calvert with 10 seconds left before the break.

Virginia was repelled again on a fourth-and-goal at the Wake Forest 5 in the fourth quarter.

Wake Forest: Hosts Merrimack next Saturday.

articles.title: No. 3 Georgia capitalizes on No. 17 Gators’ costly mistakes in 27-8 rout
articles.summary: ATLANTA — Florida’s starting quarterback didn’t matter. Georgia’s dominance against the Gators continued Saturday, whether Aaron Philo or Tramell Jones Jr. w...
articles.body:
ATLANTA — Florida's starting quarterback didn't matter.

Georgia's dominance against the Gators continued Saturday, whether Aaron Philo or Tramell Jones Jr. was at the controls during a 27-8 loss to the No. 3 Bulldogs at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta.

The performance extended Georgia's winning streak in the series to six games and showed first-year Florida coach Jon Sumrall how far his program still has to go.

As a crowd of 72,541 looked on, a slew of penalties, mental mistakes and turnovers undid Sumrall's squad. Florida entered the day with heightened expectations after its win at Texas on Oct. 17 raised hopes for another upset and the program's first win in the longstanding rivalry since 2020.

Rather than challenge the Bulldogs (7-1, 5-1 SEC), No. 17 Florida (5-3, 3-3) gifted them 17 of 24 points during an ugly first half that placed the Gators in an inescapable hole. The Gators faced their biggest halftime deficit in the series since trailing 28-3 in 2022 during Billy Napier's first season.

Saturday's performance had hints of Napier's error-prone teams and unimaginative offenses.

In the process, the Gators wasted a strong defense effort. Georgia managed just 318 yards, but didn't need to do much offensively to build an insurmountable lead.

Florida fell behind 24-0 after committing 60 yards of penalties, Philo suffered two interceptions and Jones coughed up a fumble that Georgia linebacker Chris Cole returned 66 yards for a touchdown 29 seconds before halftime. The turnover came just after the Gators had finally crossed midfield against Georgia's defense.

Before the fumble, which came on a sack by linebacker Quintavius Johnson, Jones had provided a momentary spark after Sumrall benched Philo following Florida's third series.

Cole's scoop-and-score extinguished and effectively ended any slim hopes of a comeback.

Throughout the game, Georgia's sizable talent gap, Kirby Smart's superior coaching and the Bulldogs' physicality were evident.

Smart's Bulldogs also had a bye week to prepare, and were eager to bounce back from a home loss to unranked Auburn.

Florida's defense went toe-to-toe with the SEC heavyweight Bulldogs, but received no help from the other side of the ball.

Offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner, a former Georgia quarterbacks coach under Smart from 2020-22, did little schematically to fool his former boss.

Florida also needed more from its playmakers.

Georgia held tailback Jadan Baugh to just 38 yards on 17 carries during his homecoming to the Atlanta area, where he grew up in nearby Decatur. Sophomore receiver Vernell Brown III missed his fourth straight game , ruled out before kickoff because of a lingering knee injury. Receiver Eric Singleton, a native of Atlanta, had just 19 receiving yards and dropped two passes, including a pass that went through his hands for Philo's second interception.

A penalty for sideline interference tacked on 15 yards to Florida's 17. Four plays later, Peyton Woodring was good from 28 yards for a 10-0 lead.

Earlier, Florida forced a three-and-out after a head-scratching interception by Philo while he was being sacked gave Georgia the ball on the Gators' 41. But walk-on receiver Jaden Edgecombe roughed punter Drew Miller, drawing a 15-yard flag and giving the Bulldogs the ball on the 31.

Five plays later, Bulldogs' tailback Nate Frazier punched it in from one-yard out for Georgia's first points during a long day for Florida.

Midway through the fourth quarter, the only drama remaining was whether Florida's NCAA-leading streak of scoring in 480 games, dating to 1988, would end.

An interception in the end zone by Georgia cornerback Braylon Conley had been the Gators' best chance to extend the scoring streak. But a 42-yard fumble return by linebacker Myles Graham gave Jones another opportunity to salvage something on a three-turnover day.

The 19-year-old sophomore led a nine-play, 48-yard drive, culminating with Jones' two-yard scoring run on fourth down. Baugh completed a pass to Dallas Wilson for a two-point conversion.

It was too little too late on a day the Gators wilted against the two-time SEC defending champions.

Florida ended with five turnovers and 78 yards in penalties during a nightmarish effort on Halloween.

Florida now turns its attention to November, beginning with a visit Saturday from Oklahoma. Plenty is still at stake as Sumrall continues building his program.

But he and the Gators saw the SEC's gold standard firsthand in Atlanta — and just how much ground remains between Florida and the program Smart has built in Athens.

Edgar Thompson can be reached at egthompson@orlandosentinel.com

articles.title: Moore wins Breeders' Cup Turf for record sixth time
articles.summary: Jockey Ryan Moore and trainer Aidan O'Brien both made history as they won the Breeders' Cup Turf with Benvenuto Cellini.
articles.body:
Ryan Moore won the Breeders' Cup Turf at Keeneland for a record sixth time on Saturday in Kentucky.

The English jockey triumphed in the £3.7m ($5m) feature race with Benvenuto Cellini, timing his final push perfectly and powering home by three-quarters of a lenght ahead of compatriot James Doyle on Map Of Stars in second.

It gave Irish trainer Aidan O'Brien a record-extending eighth victory in the race, with another of his horses Diamond Necklace finishing in third.

Moore was appointed MBE for services to racing and British sport in June, is widely regarded as the best jockey of his generation and rode Estimate to victory in the Gold Cup at Royal Ascot in 2013 for Queen Elizabeth II.

O'Brien, who was equalling his own record of 28 top-level victories in a calendar year, praised his horse, who was 3-1 favourite.

"He's a horse that showed a lot of class. Ryan was calm and relaxed on him and let it happen. He was brilliant on him. He did it again, he had to come out and come round," he said.

"Time after time he produces on the day. He accepted early he let them go, but he had one bullet to fire which he executed perfectly."

"It's so special that everyone is here. It's a special day."

Benvenuto Cellini's dam Newspaperofrecord herself won the Breeders' Cup in 2018.

In the Breeders' Cup Classic, Venezuelan jockey Junior Alvarado won with Sovereignty.

The four-year-old horse was scrapped from competing last year because of fever, but swept aside the competition including Japan's Forever Young who was going for his second successive win but finished in fifth.

Trained by American Bill Mott, Alvarado said his victory with Sovereignty was "spectacular".

"We really wanted to run so bad the Classic last year. I'm just so glad the Godolphin team gave us a chance to keep him in training and get to do what he did today," he said.
