After the final snap of Florida's sixth straight loss to Georgia, the Gators Wire staff submitted their instant reactions and analysis to the upset win in good, bad and ugly format. Here is what we had to offer about the carnage we witnessed in Week 9.

PHOTOS: Top highlights from Florida's 2026 rivalry game vs Georgia

GOOD : The defense looked surprisingly robust in this one, especially considering how long they were forced to remain on the field. Do not let the final score confuse you — the corps was forced to defend a short field all day long and did a great job shutting Georgia out in the third and through most of the fourth quarter.

The biggest play of the day for Florida was the Myles Graham scoop-and-run for 42 yards that ultimately led to the Gators' lone score of the day.

BAD : A loss to Georgia always smarts, but this one especially hurt because it looked like Florida just did not want to win this one. Turnovers — particularly one that I will mention below — plus dumb penalties like a roughing the punter that set up the Dawgs' first score gave the impression that the team's collective heads were just not in the game.

Sumrall has a lot to talk about with his team this week as they prepare for Oklahoma.

UGLY : Philo's underhanded interception throw in the first quarter was the dumbest, most ill-advised play I've seen from a quarterback in a long time. It is unfathomable to me that at any point during the play he thought that was a good idea.

Personally, I would have pulled him immediately if I were the head coach, but alas, a second interception finally did the trick. That level of decision-making does not belong on the field.

GOOD : Bailey Stockton provided some of Florida's most dependable offensive work. He converted two third downs on the opening second-half possession, helping the Gators escape the shadow of their own end zone, and remained a reliable target for Tramell Jones Jr. His 18-yard punt return also set Florida up in Georgia territory.

On an afternoon short on offensive positives, Stockton consistently gave the Gators something to build on.

BAD : Florida struggled to establish a running game that could keep its quarterbacks in manageable situations. Jadan Baugh repeatedly met defenders behind the line, and sacks further complicated an already difficult afternoon.

Even after the quarterback change, the same problems persisted: an encouraging completion, a backward step and another long-yardage down. Baugh's fourth-and-20 conversion was remarkable, but needing that kind of rescue illustrated how poorly the offense functioned.

UGLY : Florida's most damaging failures came when points finally looked possible. Late in the first half, Jones moved the offense into Georgia territory before a strip-sack became Chris Cole's 66-yard touchdown return. A potential halftime lift instead became a 24-0 deficit.

The Gators later reached Georgia's 3-yard line on a possession already kept alive by a roughing-the-passer penalty that erased an interception. Given another chance, Florida threw another pick. Those two possessions captured the frustration: enough progress to create hope, followed by mistakes that erased it.

GOOD : It might be difficult to find positives in a game that got away from Florida early, but the Gators' defense did enough to keep the door cracked open. After giving up 24 points in the first half, Florida held the Bulldogs scoreless in the third quarter. The problem was that Florida's offense continually put its defense in difficult situations.

For a unit that has struggled at times this season, there were at least stretches where Florida's defense gave the offense opportunities to make the game competitive.

BAD : Florida entered Saturday needing its offense to complement a defense facing one of the SEC's best teams. Instead, the Gators struggled to generate anything consistently.

Aaron Philo returned to the starting lineup after missing Florida's upset win over Texas, but his return did not provide the spark the Gators hoped for. Going 5 for 7 and throwing two interceptions resulting in Florida turning back to Tramell Jones Jr., who helped lead the upset in Austin two weeks earlier.

The running game also struggled to provide much support. Jadan Baugh has continued to struggle for the bulk of his SEC play this season, only rushing for 38 yards against Georgia.

UGLY : You cannot beat Kirby Smart and Georgia when you consistently beat yourself.

Florida's mistakes were the defining story of the afternoon. The Gators threw multiple interceptions, lost a fumble that Georgia returned for a touchdown and committed costly penalties that extended Bulldogs possessions.

Aaron Philo's irrational underhand interception started it, but the sequence before halftime perfectly summarized Florida's problems. Trailing 17-0, Jones was sacked and stripped by Quintavius Johnson; Chris Cole recovered the football and returned it 66 yards for a touchdown, turning an already difficult deficit into a 24-0 halftime hole.

Against an opponent of Georgia's caliber, there is almost no margin for error. Florida crossed that margin repeatedly Saturday, and the scoreboard reflected it.

articles.title: Georgia report card: Grading the Bulldogs after blowout of Florida
articles.summary: How did Georgia perform against Florida? We hand out grades for the offense, defense, coaching, special teams and overall performance.
articles.body:
ATLANTA-- Georgia football handled Florida with an 27-8 victory Saturday, but not every unit performed equally well.

Others raised some questions heading into next week.

Here's our postgame report card for the Bulldogs.

Georgia rushed for 213 yards on 39 carries. The Bulldogs started 1 of 5 on third downs and finished 7 of 14. Gunner Stockton was just 13 of 23 for 101 yards and had several passes batted down at the line. Coach Kirby Smart told ABC at halftime that Stockton wasn't throwing downfield on short plays. Stockton rushed for 45 yards on 12 carries.

Georgia did not have an offensive play longer than 17 yards until a deep ball for Craig Dandridge for 32 yards in the second half, but Talyn Taylor fumbled after a catch at the 14 for a turnover. Georgia had two three-and-outs to start the second half.

Georgia's defense's four turnovers led to 17 points. The Bulldogs set the tone by holding Florida to 3 yards a play in the first quarter and holding Jaden Baugh to 11 yards on 4 carries and 38 yards on 11 carries for the game. Ellis Robinson made the play for an interception on a poor decision by Aaron Philo to toss the ball up under pressure.

Georgia had 11 tackles for loss and 4 sacks and held Florida to 246 total yards.

Check out our Georgia football vs Florida photo gallery: Best images

Sacovie White-Helton had a 30-yard punt return deep in Georgia territory but muffed a bouncing third-quarter punt that he recovered. Peyton Woodring was wide right on a 43-yard field goal but converted from 28 and 21. Drew Miller averaged 49 yards on three punts and Georgia gave up 31 punt return yards to Bailey Stockton on two punts.

Taking it to your rivals who just beat a top 10 Texas team is mission accomplished. The Bulldogs cleaned up the missed tackles and came up with a stifling defensive performance. Georgia controlled the ball in the first half, doubling Florida in plays to take control.

The junior had a team-high nine tackles, a sack and returned a fumble recovery 66 yards for a touchdown.

Georgia played a cleaner game and its defense came up with timely turnovers to help out an offense that wasn't playing its best. Florida has a new coach, but the Bulldogs continue to own the Gators with a sixth straight win.

articles.title: Sovereignty reigns supreme in Breeders' Cup Classic
articles.summary: Sovereignty won Saturday's $7 million Grade I Breeders' Cup Classic over a field that included lthis year's Kentucky Derby, Belmont Stakes champion.
articles.body:
LEXINGTON, Ky., Oct. 31 Sovereignty reigned supreme in Saturday's $7 million Grade 1 Breeders' Cup Classic, rallying to win by 1 3/4 lengths over a field including last year's winner, Japanese superstar Forever Young, and Kentucky Derby and Belmont Stakes winner Golden Tempo.

Sovereignty, the 2025 Kentucky Derby, Belmont and Travers winner, was a late scratch from last year's Classic at Del Mar with an ill-timed fever. He'd been pointed toward this year's renewal ever since and made the most of the opportunity.

Forever Young chased the speedy Knightsbridge through the early furlongs with Sovereignty well off the pace and Golden Tempo, as usual, trailing the field.

As they hit the stretch, both Knightsbridge and Forever Young threw in the towel. Sovereignty picked up the baton and ran to the lead.

Golden Tempo's trademark late charge petered out and the final order of finish, after the winner, was Pennsylvania Derby winner The Puma, Knightsbridge, another Japanese runner, T O Password, and Forever Young. Golden Tempo and Napoleon Solo were the trailers.

Sovereignty, a Godolphin homebred trained by Bill Mott, finished the 1 1/4 miles in 2:00.36 with regular rider Junior Alvarado in the irons.

"When we turned into the backstretch," Alvarado said, "I was very confident the way he was traveling. ... There's no way any other horse could have come in any faster than he did."

Mott added: "I knew that if he showed up, he'd be hard to beat. just know how talented and what a train he is. I've had a couple of good ones, but you could say he's a once in a lifetime horse."

The day's other races on the Keeneland dirt track were run largely to form, including a win by a Japanese-trained colt who specializes in American raids.

Nitrogen, the 3-5 favorite, took a mid-stretch detour to the middle of the track, but still was plenty good enough to land the Distaff by 2 lengths from chief rival Fully Subscribed, improving on her second-place finish in the same race at Del Mar.

A 4-year-old Medaglia d'Oro filly, Nitrogen raced behind the early leaders into the stretch turn in the 1 1/8-mile Distaff. She rallied to the lead willingly for jockey Jose Ortiz, but wandered outward with a furlong to run, opening a big gap for Fully Subscribed.

Once Ortiz corrected the route, Nitrogen dug in and wasn't seriously threatened. She finished in 1:48.90.

A year ago, Nitrogen was unable to catch loose-on-the-lead Scylla, finishing 5 1/2 lengths back of that now-retired rival. In the interim, she posted three wins, two seconds and a third from five starts, all graded stakes, for trainer Mark Casse and owner/breeder D J Stable LLC.

Casse said the connections considered running Nitrogen in the Classic, but decided to reserve that option for her 5-year-old year. She could contest the Grade I Pegasus Invitational at Gulfstream Park in February, he said.

Jonathan Green, who currently manages D J Stable, joked at the post-race press conference that Casse's job for 2027 was to stop Nitrogen from wandering down the stretch. Casse replied: "She can wander all she wants if she keeps winning like that."

Japanese-trained T O Elvis blazed down the stretch in the 6-furlong sprint, caught breakaway favorite Englishman and easily relegated him to second by 1 1/4 lengths. Liam Smith was third, another 4 lengths back, and Hymn fourth in what the bettors accurately saw as a two-horse race.

Although T O Elvis represents Japanese owner Tomoya Ozasa (thus the name) and trains for Takayanagi, the 4-year-old colt is a Kentucky-bred by Volatile, out of the Curlin mare Stopshoppingdebbie.

His connections also went to the trouble to bring him to Kentucky early in the season and were rewarded with a victory in the Churchill Downs Stakes (G1) on May 2. Before that, he won four in a row at home, including the Grade 3 Capella Stakes at Nakayama Racecourse.

Ozasa and Takayanagi enthusiastically agreed American racing fans can expect to see T O Elvis again in the 2027 season.

Englishman, a 3-year-old Maxfield colt trained by Cherie DeVaux, had four wins from five starts before the Sprint, but had not raced since winning the Grade I H. Allen Jerkens at Saratoga on Aug. 29. His only previous defeat came in the Grade II Pat Day Mile at Churchill Downs, when he faded from the lead to finish second.

The race was 1 mile long, but the margin of victory was a nose -- a whisker, really, as odds-on favorite Further Ado nipped Owen Almighty in the final stride of the Dirt Mile.

It appeared briefly that Further Ado had met the challenge after a stretch-long battle as he lunged for the finish. But it was not quite enough to deny Further Ado, a 3-year-old Gun Runner colt who won the Grade I Blue Grass at Keeneland by 11 lengths on his way to a start in the Kentucky Derby.

The colt also scored his first career win at Keeneland last October -- by 20 lengths. Further Ado, with Flavien Prat up for trainer Brad Cox, finished in 1:34.50.

Further Ado was left as favorite in the race when two other candidates, Knightsbridge and Napoleon Solo, opted for the Classic. Owner Eric Gustavson said the decision between races was hard.

"He wants more distance. He's a mile and an eighth guy. But you have to go one way or the other so we're just happy it worked out," he said.

Ways and Means, the even-money favorite, saved ground through the turn in the Filly & Mare Sprint, came out to exploit a big opening between rivals and shot away to win by 6 1/4 lengths.

The Practical Joke mare, with Flavien Prat riding for trainer Chad Brown and Klaravich Stables, finished 7 furlongs out of the backstretch chute in 1:21.76.

It was her fourth win from her last five starts and avenged a fifth-place finish in the 2025 edition at Del Mar. Foie Gras was best of the rest with Explora and Kilwin in the minor placings.

articles.title: Tommy Carr fights through flu to power Michigan: 'He's tough as nails'
articles.summary: Tommy Carr dealt with the flu during the week and had some rough moments, but no one would have known during Michigan's 28-21 win at Rutgers.
articles.body:
PISCATAWAY, N.J. — Michigan freshman quarterback Tommy Carr dealt with the flu during the week and had some rough moments, but no one would have known during the Wolverines' 28-21 victory at Rutgers considering his performance.

Carr accounted for 320 total yards and three total touchdowns, including two rushing, in his second straight start since taking over for sophomore Bryce Underwood. Underwood had started 19 games but lost the job to Carr in the second half of the Penn State game two weeks ago.

The Wolverines (5-3, 2-3 Big Ten) will face Michigan State next weekend at Michigan Stadium.

"He was not feeling good, but he didn't miss any practice," Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham said of Carr. "He's a tough kid. You talk about a guy that's tough as nails, Tommy Carr is tough as nails both mentally and physically. He wasn't feeling good at all, particularly, I think it was the Thursday practice. But he was out there and battling and didn't miss a beat. He was pretty sick at points in the week."

Carr was 22 of 27 passing for 266 yards and a touchdown. He rushed for 54 yards on 12 carries and scored two touchdowns, including the winning 9-yard run on a broken play.

"I think a lot of it comes down to being young and just playing in the backyard and just making people miss," Carr said of his knack for scrambling and making plays. "Did that a lot when I was younger, but then just being able to make throws off the platform and just making plays with your legs."

Whittingham would not say earlier in the week who the starting quarterback would be, but it is clear this is Carr's job going forward.

"I felt he took a big step forward this week, without a doubt," Whittingham said. "Shoot, he was over 80% completion percentage. His legs came up with some big runs for us. Couple touchdowns, 50 - something yards in rushing, took care of the football. No turnovers. Made a bunch of first downs. Possessed the ball for nearly 40 minutes. So yeah, he was instrumental in all that good stuff happening."

Carr said there were a couple deep balls, both underthrown, he'd like to get back, but he felt good about his progress.

"If we'd have been on the right on the money — that's easy to say — but if he was able to drop it out there where it needed to be, I think they both would have been touchdowns or at least huge gains," Whittingham said. "I'm not sure that is indicative of his arm strength. I just think he needs to get the ball just a hair quicker and put a little more on it because he does have an arm. Doesn't have a Bryce Underwood arm, but he's got an arm that's very capable."

Carr is still about 20 pounds lighter than Whittingham said is ideal, and with those weight gains will come strength gains. But Carr's intangibles include his poise.

"That's one of his strengths," Whittingham said. "He's unflappable. He never panics. He's very calm, collected, no matter what the situation, and that's a great quality to have in a quarterback. I mean, he's a guy that already you know the moment is not too big for him. I think I said that last week, and it showed up again this week.

"And his pocket presence was outstanding. I thought he moved around well in the pocket, kept his eyes downfield a bunch of the time to find some receivers and tucked it and ran when he needed to. So, a lot of good things by Tommy."

Two starts have allowed Carr to build confidence.

"You get more comfortable with the more experience that you have," Carr said. "Still got to hit a few deep balls. Just get better each and every week."

articles.title: Stützle, Cozens lead Senators past Sharks 5-1 as Ottawa ties franchise record with nine October wins
articles.summary: (AP) — Tim Stützle and Dylan Cozens each had a goal and an assist and the Ottawa Senators defeated the San Jose Sharks 5-1 on Saturday.The Senators snapped a...
articles.body:
SAN JOSE, Calif. (AP) — Tim Stützle and Dylan Cozens each had a goal and an assist and the Ottawa Senators defeated the San Jose Sharks 5-1 on Saturday.

The Senators snapped a two-game skid and matched the franchise record for October victories with their ninth, equaling the mark set in 2007-08. Ottawa lost the first two games of a five-game trip that continues in Anaheim on Sunday.

Drake Batherson, Ridly Greig and Shane Pinto also scored for Ottawa, while Samuel Ersson made 21 saves.

Michael Misa scored the lone goal for the Sharks and Alex Nedeljkovic stopped 30 shots.

Ottawa broke open a 1-1 game with three second-period goals. Batherson put the Senators ahead at 5:04 before Stützle and Greig scored 1:23 apart midway through the stanza.

Cozens opened the scoring at 13:25 of the first period, and Misa tied it at 16:06 with his third goal of the season.

Stützle finished October with nine goals and 12 assists, extending his franchise record for points in the month to 21. He finished one goal shy of Bob Kudelski's team October record, established in 1993.

Batherson extended his point streak to seven games, scoring his ninth goal of the season. Cozens scored for the third time in two games after scoring twice in Thursday's 6-5 overtime loss at Los Angeles.

Ersson earned his first victory of the season after entering 0-3-1. Ottawa has been without injured goaltender Linus Ullmark.

The Senators improved to 9-5-1 and split the two-game season series after losing 6-2 at home on Oct. 22.

San Jose fell to 7-7-1 and lost for the third time in four games.

articles.title: Trading for Jonathan Taylor would be big mistake for 1 team
articles.summary: Acquiring Taylor would be a bad move for this franchise.
articles.body:
The Jonathan Taylor NFL trade rumors are heating up, and the star running back is expected to be moved. The Indianapolis Colts have already traded Quenton and Deforest Buckner, so another star player being moved makes even more sense now.

Will the Colts actually move on from Jonathan Taylor, though? The latest reports indicate they are willing to, and two teams are most often linked to Taylor. One of those teams will be making a big mistake if they trade for Taylor, though.

Vikings and Giants are top suitors for Taylor

It seems to be a tug-of-war battle between the Giants and Vikings. Which team is going to move multiple draft picks for the running back? The Vikings are undefeated, and their offense has not been strong. There is room with Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason. Adding Jonathan Taylor will elevate this team significantly.

The Giants have a head coach in John Harbaugh who has been pushing to grab a high-end running back. They wanted Jerimayeh Love in the draft, and the team offered Kenneth Walker III a deal in free agency. This team is 4-2-1 and has a legitimate chance at winning the NFC East.

This may be a mistake for this team. Is the running back position the only spot that needs to be filled for this team to be a contender? The answer is no. QB Jaxson Dart is out for the season, while both Brian Burns and Tremaine Edmunds are out for the season on the defensive side of things.

The Giants need to fix their run defense more than adding to their rush offense. Yes, their defense as a whole is much improved, but the defensive tackles need to be upgraded, and more depth is most important. Shipping off numerous draft picks for a running back seems like they would be addressing the wrong issue.

Taking a measured approach to the rebuild is essential for this franchise. The focus should be on constructing a team that can compete for the long term, rather than making short-sighted moves for a single season that may not yield significant results due to talent deficiencies in key positions. Are the Giants really considering parting with multiple draft picks, such as a 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th, similar to the Christian McCaffrey trade?

John Harbaugh is eager to enhance this roster swiftly and has expressed a clear desire for a running back capable of handling 25+ carries. While Cam Skattebo showed promise with a solid performance against the Texans, he may not be the long-term solution.

Trading draft picks for a running back could seem beneficial now, especially considering the potential of Malik Nabers, Isaiah Likely, and Jaxson Dart in the future. However, the team still faces significant challenges, and acquiring a running back at the trade deadline may not have the impact you anticipate.

Earlier this season, Haas confirmed that Esteban Ocon's time with the team would end following the 2026 Formula 1 season, with Rafael Câmara confirmed for his seat next season.

Intrigue around Ocon and that seat has only heightened in the last few hours, with Haas announcing hours before qualifying at the Mexico City Grand Prix that Ocon will not be in the car for the rest of the weekend, with reserve driver Ryō Hirakawa taking the seat for qualifying, and then Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix. Hirakawa, who drove in FP1 on Friday, will now be making his F1 debut:

Friday's FP1 session in Mexico City was Hirakawa's third practice outing of the 2026 F1 season.

On the Thursday ahead of the United States Grand Prix in Austin Ocon told the media, including SB Nation, that he should be in F1 next season.

"As I said, I deserve to be here in Formula One. There are many circumstances why I'm not here next year, but they are not the performance reasons," said Ocon in Austin last week. "I've won everything that I've in every category I've done in go-kart, in Formula Renault, in Formula 3, in GP3 in F1 In all these categories I've won races, so just, you know, thinking of a sports perspective, I deserve to be in F1.

"Yeah, I believe that this is not my last year."

What adds to the speculation about Ocon's future is how that statement from the team ends: No further statements will be made at this time.

This could certainly be an illness-related absence. Kimi Antonelli and Sergio Pérez missed portions of this week already due to illness and fatigue, and the grind of the F1 season could be taking a toll on Ocon as well.

Although Haas has reportedly denied that it is illness related:

And with Ocon already on his way out at Haas, it is also possible that the team has moved up his departure. Haas currently sits seventh in the F1 Constructors' Championship standings with 30 points, 39 points behind sixth-place Alpine.

Adam Cooper, a fixture in the paddock, noted that Ocon did have a disagreement with his team over tire usage during FP2 on Friday:

Cooper then clipped part of the exchange between Ocon and his engineer, Laura Müller:

If Haas indeed makes the switch to Câmara, it could put the Brazilian driver in line to make his F1 debut at his home race, next weekend's São Paulo Grand Prix. Câmara currently leads the F2 Drivers' Championship standings with 207 points, seven points ahead of second-place Nikola Tsolov, and with F2 not set to race again until Qatar and Abu Dhabi to close out the season — if those races in deed take place — there might be a window to make such a switch.

articles.title: Esteban Ocon issues statement after Haas benching, denies physical altercation rumours
articles.summary: Esteban Ocon has issued his first statement addressing media rumours around his falling out with Haas at Formula 1's Mexico City Grand Prix
articles.body:
Dropped Haas Formula 1 driver Esteban Ocon has denied French media rumours of a physical altercation with team boss Ayao Komatsu as he issued his response to missing this weekend's Mexico Grand Prix.

Ocon was benched in Mexico, most likely connected to a public disagreement with his race engineer during free practice. That led to a discussion with the team on Friday night as the relationship between the Frenchman and his team has become increasingly strained.

As a result of Friday's events, details of which remain sparse, Haas made the decision to drop Ocon for the remainder of the weekend, with reserve driver and Toyota WEC driver Ryo Hirakawa taking over his car from FP3 onwards.

But with speculation rife in French media outlets over the exact nature of Ocon's spat with Komatsu, including rumours of a possible physical altercation between the two, Ocon's camp was forced to deny those unsubstantiated rumours via his social media accounts.

"Following the recent decision from Haas F1 Team confirming that I will not be participating in this weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix, I wish to formally address some media reports and speculation surrounding the situation," Ocon's accounts posted.

"Last night, a difference in viewpoints led to a discussion with the parties involved. Whilst I acknowledge that this took place, I categorically reject any reports or allegations suggesting that any form of physical violence was used to resolve any differences of any nature."

He added: "I strongly condemn violence in all its forms and firmly believe that disagreements should always be handled with professionalism, respect, and mutual understanding. I kindly ask that speculation be avoided while the matter is being addressed. Further updates will be communicated in due course."

At this point it isn't yet clear if Ocon will return to the car at next weekend's Brazilian Grand Prix or if he will finish the season with the US-owned team at all.

The 30-year-old grand prix winner is fighting for his F1 future after being dropped for 2027 for Ferrari rookie Rafa Camara, with options to remain in F1 dwindling rapidly.

articles.title: Trick & Treat: Unique formations spark Monmouth football to 6th straight win
articles.summary: Monmouth (7-2) raced out to an early 24-0 lead and never looked back as the team cruised to a 34-21 win over Bryant (5-4) on Saturday.
articles.body:
WEST LONG BRANCH -- Monmouth football broke out the tricks with the treats this Halloween, and the Hawks had the Bryant defense seeing ghosts all Saturday afternoon at Kessler Stadium.

After hitting the road on six of their first eight games, the FCS No. 17 Hawks came home for the holiday and delivered an emphatic victory - their sixth straight - in their return. With several unique running designs to spark the offense, Monmouth (7-2) raced out to an early 24-0 lead and never looked back as the team cruised to a 34-21 victory.

"I was very happy with how we played in all three phases. Guys had great energy. I thought we were the more physical team today, and that was a dangerous team," Monmouth head coach Jeff Gallo said. "We did a really good job from the start. We're trying to make it known what it's like to play us here at home."

After a relatively slow start in the first half in a dominant 49-13 win over Hampton last week, the Hawks wasted no time setting the tone against Bryant (5-4) at home. On the opening drive, the Hawks marched 75 yards to the end zone before finishing the possession with a first glimpse at their offensive innovation: a pistol formation with the quarterback motioning out to receiver to reveal a wildcat formation. Elijah Jennings took the snap and ran a counter right up the middle for an 18-yard touchdown.

"Just banking those reps all week," center Kevin Shriner said. "It's really a shout out to our scout team, giving us a great look. It's a great job by the running backs rotating, no matter who's back there taking the wildcat, I know they're going to get through."

All four of Monmouth's touchdowns came on some variation of that wildcat offensive concept, including two explosive touchdown runs of 37 and 55 yards in the first half that put the game firmly in the grasp of the Hawks by halftime. It was another banner day for the team's dynamic backfield duo, as Jennings finished with 167 yards and two touchdowns on 20 carries while Kenny Smith Jr. had 162 yards and two scores on 18 runs.

Combined with a lights out defensive performance for three quarters and a strong day for the much-improved special teams unit, highlighted by two field goals by Sky Sholder, the Hawks were unquestionably the superior team against a Bryant squad that had emerged as a potential contender for the conference title before losing to Stony Brook last week.

"Skyler's done a great job," Gallo said. "When it's time to kick a field goal, we trust that he can get those points. I think in general, our special teams coach Dennis Long has done a great job of improving every week. We've gotten better every week. Our kickoff team is really fun to watch right now, and we found some good returns."

The Monmouth defense delivered an early dagger with an interception by Omar Ibrahim on Bryant's first play from scrimmage in the second half. It was both a steady defensive performance and one shaped by the Hawks' ability to generate negative plays.

"We preach it all week, every week: we want to start fast and finish faster," linebacker Charlie Sasso said. "We want to start the game exactly how we did. We obviously want a better finish to the game than we had. Our coaches put us in a great spot to really finish through practice every day, and I think that's transitioning over to games where we're playing harder in the fourth quarter."

The Bulldogs got two fourth quarter touchdowns, including one with 27 seconds remaining, to add some window dressing to the result. But it was arguably the best performance of the season for the Monmouth defense, which held Bryant to 94 rushing yards and 39 passing yards through the first three quarters. Linebacker Ryan Russo was another individual star in the game, finishing with two sacks.

"He works harder than anybody I know. We have team lifts every week, he's lifting extra on his own every week. He's in at night lifting, he's at home doing recovery," Sasso said. "He puts everything into this that he has and it really shows in the way he plays."

The lone blemish was the modest passing game, which was scarcely needed given the dominance on the ground. Quarterback Frankie Weaver finished 10-for-20 for 81 passing yards with no touchdowns or interceptions. It was Monmouth's lowest passing yardage total in a victory since 2002.

"We're going to try to be balanced all the time. And balance means we can throw it when we want to throw it and run it when we want to run it," Gallo said. "We were having success early. We could stay with that. These guys did a great job of finding holes, and there were also some long explosive runs, which set us up for great success. But we're going to continue to fight to be balanced."

Ultimately, balance wasn't necessary Saturday given the Hawks ability to bulldoze their way to a victory against a Bryant front that was rated highly coming into the matchup.

"It fires us up every time. Everybody's working as one, everybody's on the same page," offensive guard Reed Collins said. "Seeing them bust those long runs gets us really excited and we're gonna be a really exciting offense as we keep going forward."

Monmouth's 319 rushing yards were a testament to work of the offensive line, although they did concede two sacks after not allowing one through 507 snaps. It's proof the team still has more room to grow, a good point of motivation to counterbalance the team's immense success through the first two months of the season.

"I'm proud of how hard these guys work every week," Gallo said. "There's still a lot of football left, and we're gonna focus NC A&T and that's a one-week season. And that's what I'm proud of these guys to be able to do is compartmentalize—learn from the win or the loss and then focus on the next opponent. That's what I'm the most proud of and we've done a good job of that and we're gonna keep doing that."

The Hawks now sit alone atop the CAA standings with a 6-0 record in conference play, the last unbeaten team. No. 25 Albany, the team that ruined Monmouth's playoff bid a year ago, has emerged as an unlikely ally of sorts after toppling No. 15 Campbell in a 45-35 win. Monmouth beat Albany 28-20 on Sept. 19, which means the Hawks have the clear path to their first conference title since 2019 and their first as a member of the Coastal Athletic Association.

Monmouth also knows all too well the pain of being undercut by a loss late in the season after that season-ending loss to Albany last November. With three games left, there's still plenty of room for variables. With two upcoming games against teams with losing records, it might seem like a manageable slate. But the double-edged sword means any losses would be more damaging to the Hawks' playoff hopes.

As this week's results demonstrated, there are no guarantees in the CAA. And next week's opponent, North Carolina A&T (4-5) has now won three straight games.

"We said it all offseason. Our motto was leave no doubt," Sasso said. "We don't want to leave anything up to anyone else other than how we perform on the field."

articles.title: Lincoln Kienholz has 3 total touchdowns to lead Louisville past Stanford 52-24
articles.summary: (AP) — Lincoln Kienholz threw for 250 yards, two touchdowns and rushed for another score to lead Louisville to a 52-24 win over Stanford on Saturday.Louisvil...
articles.body:
LOUISVILLE, Ky. (AP) — Lincoln Kienholz threw for 250 yards, two touchdowns and rushed for another score to lead Louisville to a 52-24 win over Stanford on Saturday.

Louisville (5-3, 4-2 Atlantic Coast Conference) recorded its first win over the Cardinal and extended Stanford's road losing streak to 15 games, the longest active skid in the FBS.

The Cardinals scored on back-to-back turnovers and outscored Stanford 21-7 in the third quarter to break the game open. Stanford led twice in the second quarter and tied the score at 24 in the third quarter before the hosts pulled away by scoring 28 unanswered points.

Tre Richardson caught 10 passes for 140 yards for Louisville, which amassed 545 yards of offense, a balance of 249 yards through the air and 296 rushing. Isaac Brown led Louisville with 139 yards rushing and scored on a 75-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter.

Davis Warren threw for 270 yards and three touchdowns for the Cardinal (4-5, 2-4), including a 75-yard touchdown pass to Aiden Black in the second quarter.

Stanford: The Cardinal fell to 0-4 in road games this season. Stanford had been outscored 150-17 in the previous three road games and matched that total in the first half. Stanford was averaging 5.8 points and 212 yards per game on the road prior to Saturday. Stanford had scored just 17 points in three previous road games, but surpassed that total against the Cardinals.

Louisville: Coach Jeff Brohm improved to 5-1 in games following a bye week. the Cardinals were without leading wide receiver Lawayne McCoy, who will be out for an "extended time" because of a knee injury. McCoy caught 25 passes for 513 yards and four touchdowns in the team's first seven games. The Cardinals, fourth in the nation in average yards per carry at 5.9, had nine yards per carry on Saturday.

Louisville: at Georgia Tech next Saturday.

articles.title: 3 takeaways from the Jazz’s Halloween horror show against the Blazers
articles.summary: The Jazz couldn't overcome 20n turnovers, poor shooting and Portland's physical defense, falling to 1-4 at home at the Delta Center.
articles.body:
I promise the Utah Jazz are trying to win games this season, even if it didn't look like it Saturday afternoon.

Utah suffered one of its worst performances of the young season in front of the Jazz faithful, falling 112-90 to the Portland Trail Blazers at the Delta Center.

The Jazz never really found their footing, as they trailed by double-digits for a majority of the afternoon and failed to put together a meaningful run to make things interesting.

Maybe it was the early 1 p.m. start. Maybe it was Halloween festivities on the mind. Maybe it was simply a bad day at the office. Whatever the reason, there wasn't much to like about this one.

Here are three takeaways from Utah's loss.

A Halloween horror show from the opening tip

The Jazz couldn't have gotten off to a much worse start.

Utah opened the afternoon shooting just 3 of 14 from the field and watched Portland put together a 17-0 run in the first quarter. Even more surprising was that coach Will Hardy didn't call a timeout during the entire stretch.

The Jazz eventually found some offense through their bench and managed to cut the deficit to nine points by the end of the first quarter, but the damage was already done.

The second quarter wasn't much better. The Blazers opened with another 7-0 run, and Utah struggled to generate anything consistently on the offensive end.

Before the game, Hardy acknowledged that his young players have been dealing with some stress and uncertainty as they try to establish themselves in the league.

"There's sort of like an uncertainty of where they fit in the league," Hardy said. "We're very unproven, and I think that does lead to some anxiety in different moments."

He also mentioned that some of the poor body language fans have seen comes from frustration when the work players put in during practice and film sessions doesn't immediately translate to wins.

Saturday was a pretty clear example. There was a noticeable lack of energy throughout the game, whether it was the body language on the court or the quiet huddles during timeouts.

The Jazz looked like a team that couldn't find an answer.

Turnovers and physicality continue to haunt the Jazz

The Jazz have struggled to find consistent offense this season without center Jusuf Nurkic, and Saturday was another reminder of how important his presence is.

Nurkic is arguably Utah's best passer, and his absence has put additional pressure on a young group of guards to create offense and get everyone involved.

The Jazz had several stretches Saturday in which the ball movement disappeared, possessions ended with poor shots and Portland's defensive pressure made it difficult for Utah to even get into its halfcourt offense.

Hardy actually addressed the team's turnover problems before the game, pointing out how quickly a few mistakes can derail an entire stretch.

"I think turnovers as the game has gone on has hurt us," Hardy said. "I think we're seeing pockets where it's three and four turnovers in, you know, five or six possessions."

That problem showed up again Saturday afternoon. Utah finished with 20 turnovers, and the Blazers' physical defense consistently bothered the Jazz's ball handlers.

After the game, Hardy noted the team's inability to take care of the ball continues to be a major problem.

"Our ability to be solid with the ball is continuing to haunt us," Hardy said, "and you couple that with a night where you can't make a 3."

The Jazz shot poorly again from deep, going 11-40 from beyond the arc.

But Hardy wasn't interested in blaming everything on poor shooting. He said Utah struggled with both its shot-making and its overall offensive execution.

"I don't think we played very good," Hardy said. "I think the ball pressure bothered us, our screening wasn't very good, our ability to handle the ball pressure ... that 48 minutes of offense, for sure, is not up to the standard."

Surprisingly, with the way the game was going, the Jazz did finish with more assists than turnovers, but 20 giveaways are difficult to overcome, particularly when the team is struggling to generate quality looks.

The Jazz still have to figure out their defensive discipline

This might be the most interesting takeaway from Saturday.

Despite the lopsided score, Hardy actually felt his team defended well enough to win.

"I thought we guarded well enough to win the game," Hardy said.

He pointed to Utah's ability to protect the paint and rebound as positives, but acknowledged that the team still has to clean up its fouling, particularly when defenders get their hands caught on opposing players.

"The first half, the fouling was a little bit out of control," Hardy said. "We're not getting a bad whistle. ... We're fouling."

That's an important distinction for a young team that is still learning how to defend at this level. The Jazz can't afford to give opponents easy trips to the free-throw line while trying to establish a defensive identity.

Portland on Saturday shot 41 free throws, the most an opponent has went to the strip this season. The Blazers' two best players in Damian Lillard and Deni Avdija got to the paint at ease when they were attacking the rim.

Hardy also pointed to Portland's physicality as a major reason for his team's offensive struggles. The Blazers' pressure disrupted the Jazz's rhythm, and Utah struggled to create and maintain advantages.

"We need better screening, and then when we do have the advantage, we can't give it back," Hardy said.

The Blazers built their advantage to as many as 26 points in the third quarter, and Utah never put together a serious run to get back into the game. They were outrebounded, outmuscled and outcoached.

The Jazz are a young team, and Hardy knows there will be lessons from nights like Saturday, but learning from losses only matters if the team starts showing improvement.

Saturday was a reminder that this team has plenty of work to do as it enters a 1-5 hole to start the season.

Next up is a rematch against San Antonio.

articles.title: Ousseni Bouda has early goal and assist to lead Earthquakes to 2-1 victory over Real Salt Lake
articles.summary: (AP) — Ousseni Bouda had a goal and an assist in the first 17 minutes and the San Jose Earthquakes held on to beat Real Salt Lake 2-1 on Saturday.San Jose (1...
articles.body:
SAN JOSE, Calif. (AP) — Ousseni Bouda had a goal and an assist in the first 17 minutes and the San Jose Earthquakes held on to beat Real Salt Lake 2-1 on Saturday.

San Jose (14-9-10) moved up two spots to third place in the Western Conference with one match remaining in the regular season. The top four teams in each conference earn home-field advantage for the best-of-3 first round.

The Earthquakes jumped in front in the 2nd minute on an unassisted goal by Bouda off a free kick. Seven of Bouda's 12 career goals over 102 appearances have come this season in 32 matches.

Bouda and Preston Judd set up defender Benji Kikanovic for his first netter since 2024 and the Earthquakes took a two-goal lead in the 17th minute. Four of Bouda's five career assists have come this season. Judd notched his career-high third to go with a career-best and team-high 16 goals.

Real Salt Lake cut it to 2-1 in the 23rd minute on a goal by first-year defender Juan Manuel Sanabria — his second. Defender Sam Junqua earned his career-best third assist and Saba Lobjanidze collected his fifth in his first season with the club after making 85 appearances for Atlanta United over four seasons.

Earl Edwards Jr. finished with three saves in his third start this season for San Jose, which improves to 7-5-5 at home.

Rafael Cabral stopped three shots for Real Salt Lake (12-15-6) — now 3-11-3 on the road.

The loss, coupled with the Los Angeles Galaxy's 4-1 victory over Austin FC, knocks Real Salt Lake out of a playoff spot heading to Decision Day.

Six teams began the day vying for the final three berths.

Salt Lake: Hosts Los Angeles FC to close out the regular season on Saturday.

San Jose: At Minnesota United on Saturday to finish the regular season.

articles.title: Northville continues its run of boys' soccer success in Class D with another Section 2 title
articles.summary: Four different players scored goals for No. 6-ranked Northville
articles.body:
QUEENSBURY - Two consecutive sectional titles was quite an accomplishment for the Northville boys' soccer program, yet senior standout Nico Sevastakis envisioned even more success this fall for the Falcons.

"I knew we had a good group again this season," Sevastakis said. "I am just glad we came out again and capitalized."

Saturday started a bit slowly for the offensive juggernaut, which was the top seed in the Section 2 Class D tournament. Once things got going, though, the Falcons could not be stopped.

Northville made it three straight Class D championships as it cruised to a 5-0 victory over third-seeded Hartford at Queensbury High School.

The win by the Falcons (18-1), ranked No. 6 in the state, came in their 16th shutout of the season. Only three teams have scored this season against Northville, the first being Hartford in a 4-1 triumph for the Falcons on Sept. 5.

On Saturday, sophomore defender Magnus Halloran opened the scoring for the Falcons with 4:50 remaining in the opening half. In all, four players tallied goals for the No. 1 seed.

"Our goal from Day 1 is to be the best we can be every day," Northville coach Steve Clapper said. "They push each other to get better every day. This is not just about one person."

Northville's overall depth, talent and precision were on display throughout the 80 minutes played Saturday.

"I knew once we put one in, it was going to be a wrap," Sevastakis said. "I know we are a good group. We play very calm. We don't care about the scoreboard. We just play our game."

The lone loss this season for Northville came in a 2-1 setback against Chazy on Oct. 2.

"There were things we could learn from and get better at. We did exactly that," Clapper said. "We tightened up what we needed to tighten up. We've made our changes and now we are ready to move forward."

Just 46 seconds following the opening goal from Halloran, sophomore Ryder Wright made it 2-0 Northville on a score with 4:04 remaining before intermission. Hartford (14-4-1) was unable to muster any offense to make a comeback.

"They stuck to the game plan," Clapper said regarding his squad not being flustered by being unable to score early, despite dominating play. "It shows a level of maturity."

Just about any player that hit the field Saturday for the Falcons excelled, but Sevastakis paced the balanced offensive attack with his 12th and 13th goals of the season.

The senior's second goal came with 15:51 remaining to make it 4-0.

articles.title: Tage Thompson scores twice as Sabres extend road point streak to 7 with 3-2 win over Kings
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES (AP) — Tage Thompson scored twice, including the go-ahead goal with 6:20 remaining, and the Buffalo Sabres beat the Los Angeles Kings 3-2 on Satu...
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Tage Thompson scored twice, including the go-ahead goal with 6:20 remaining, and the Buffalo Sabres beat the Los Angeles Kings 3-2 on Saturday to extend their road point streak to seven games.

Jack Quinn had a goal and an assist, Zach Benson and Rasmus Dahlin each had two assists, and the Sabres won their third straight overall. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen made 27 saves.

Corey Perry had a power-play goal, Andre Lee also scored and Anton Forsberg stopped 28 shots for the Kings.

Thompson put the Sabres back in front on a one-timer off a pass from Quinn on a power play at 13:40 of the third period. Buffalo had controlled long stretches of the game before allowing the Kings to get back into it by taking some unnecessary penalties.

Buffalo controlled the first period but only led 1-0 on Quinn's eighth goal when he scored on a power play at 6:35.

Even with Los Angeles gaining momentum in the second half of the second period, the Sabres made it 2-0 on Thompson's ninth with 4:22 left.

Perry got the Kings on the board on a power play with 2:36 to go, though they needed a coach's challenge to overturn a goaltender interference call. Lee tied it 1:29 into the third.

The Kings were without top forward Adrian Kempe, who is day to day because of an undisclosed injury. Martin Chromiak made his NHL debut, taking Kempe's place on the first line and the power play.

Sabres: Host the Ottawa Senators on Wednesday.

articles.title: Raiola throws for 3 TDs to help Oregon beat No. 20 Northwestern 34-26
articles.summary: (AP) — Dylan Raiola completed 22 of 31 passes for 336 yards and three touchdowns to help Oregon rally to beat No. 20 Northwestern 34-26 on Saturday.
articles.body:
EUGENE, Ore. (AP) — Dylan Raiola completed 22 of 31 passes for 336 yards and three touchdowns to help Oregon rally to beat No. 20 Northwestern 34-26 on Saturday.

Raiola made his second straight start for the Ducks (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten) with Dante Moore ruled out for the season.

After Oregon running back Jordon Davison left the game with an injury in the first half, freshman Brandon Smith led the comeback with 82 yards rushing and scored the go-ahead touchdown in the fourth quarter.

Aidan Chiles was 22 of 38 for 281 yards and a touchdown for Northwestern (6-2, 3-2). He ran for 93 yards and another TD late in the second quarter, his 10th of the season.

Northwestern had a 10-0 first-quarter lead was up 20-13 at the half after Raiola's 10-yard touchdown pass to Dakorien Moore with 49 seconds remaining. Raiola hit Moore again in the fourth quarter on a 75-yard strike, with Moore finishing with 128 yards the two TDs.

Raiola found Jamari Johnson was a 17-yard touchdown pass, and Smith rushed for a 2-yard touchdown on fourth-and-goal to put Oregon ahead for the first time, 27-23, in the fourth quarter before Moore's second touchdown sealed the game.

Oregon: At No. 2 Ohio State next Saturday.

articles.title: Final Fantasy Football Week 8 Projections & Rankings: Latest Changes for Key Injuries
articles.summary: Week 8 fantasy football projections for QB, RB, WR, and TE's accounting for key injuries.
articles.body:
Below are my final projections for Week 8 fantasy football. I've accounted for injuries and depth chart changes, among other key factors. AJ Brown is inactive, along with DeVonta Smith, TreVeyon Henderson, and others. Amid those designations, sleepers have arisen from the depths of the rankings.

No major changes occur at quarterback. However, sleepers are definitely available. Geno Smith and Malik Willis are among the best non-QB1 picks this week.

D'Andre Swift is in prime position for a top-5 week now that Kyle Monangai has been ruled inactive.

Tony Pollard is borderline an RB1 in fantasy football due to the inactive status of Tyjae Spears.

Rhamondre Stevenson will benefit from TreVeyon Henderson's return. However, his backup, Corey Kiner, is an even more interesting deep-sleeper prospect. He has outplayed Henderson in recent weeks. I would not start Kiner this week, but in very deep formats and DFS, Kiner is worth a shot for 10+ touches.

Jaydon Blue might get some run as Saquon Barkley's backup. The Eagles lack depth now that four running backs are on injured reserve. It will be interesting to see how the Eagles manage to decide on a backup in the future, whether Blue or someone else.

Rashee Rice will play this week. That will cut into Cyrus Allen's playing time and reduce any value Xavier Worthy might have had. Rice and Travis Kelce are the only startable Chiefs pass-catchers you can start against the Broncos.

Kyle Williams benefits from AJ Brown's inactive status. Williams is the sole, exclusive perimeter receiver on the Patriots' current depth chart. Efton Chism III also rises a bit as he plays a hybrid slot-outside role.

Darius Cooper is definitely worth a start this week in a Flex role. He is among my top deep-sleepers this week. Cooper has played a massive snap count when DeVonta Smith has been out.

Dallas Goedert has skyrocketed with DeVonta Smith out. Whether you agree with his TE5 designation or not, Goedert is certainly startable. He could be the Eagles' No. 1 pass-catcher this Sunday.

Kyle Pitts has caught five passes in each of his last three games. Michael Penix Jr. seems to have built rapport with Pitts, and our projections have reflected his rise, making him the TE12.

Dalton Kincaid is expected to play, but his rib injury is also expected to limit his ability.

articles.title: Hillstead has a pair of scores, defense dominates as Utah State tops Colorado State 31-14
articles.summary: LOGAN, Utah (AP) — McCae Hillstead threw for a touchdown and ran for another and the Utah State defense had a dominant first half in a 31-14 win over Colorad...
articles.body:
LOGAN, Utah (AP) — McCae Hillstead threw for a touchdown and ran for another and the Utah State defense had a dominant first half in a 31-14 win over Colorado State on Saturday.

With rushing touchdowns from Nehemiah Washington of 31 yards and Hillstead of 18, the Aggies led 17-0 at halftime. At that point, the Rams had 67 total yards, minus-5 on the ground, and only had three snaps across midfield.

Javen Jacobs added a 12-yard rushing touchdown before Colorado State got on the board with a 10-play, 75-yard drive, capped by Durell Robinson's 6-yard run.

Utah State (4-5, 3-2 Pac 12) put together its fifth drive of between 70 and 75 yards with Hillstead finding Kaina Watson for a 7-yard score.

The Rams (3-6, 1-4) closed it out with a 21-yard touchdown pass from Hauss Hejny to Cedric Ross, ending a 73-yard drive.

The Aggies piled up 464 yards, led by Hillstead with 173 passing and 79 rushing, and held the ball for 36 minutes.

Colorado State had 263 yards and lost two fumbles. Robinson had 66 yards on the ground and Hejny threw for 186.

Colorado State: home against No. 20 Boise State next Saturday.

Utah State: home against Fresno State next Saturday.

articles.title: Hamilton takes first pole for Ferrari at Mexico City Grand Prix
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton takes his first pole position for Ferrari and his first for more than three years at the Mexico City Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Lewis Hamilton has claimed his first pole position for Ferrari and his first for more than three years at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

The seven-time F1 champion beat Mercedes' George Russell by 0.009 seconds as the two drivers who can potentially stop Kimi Antonelli clinching the world title on Sunday locked out the front row.

Antonelli qualified fifth behind Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Red Bull's Max Verstappen, but will start fourth because of a one-place penalty for the Dutchman.

The only way Antonelli can be prevented from winning the title is if Russell wins and the Italian finishes lower than ninth, or if Hamilton wins and Antonelli is out of the points.

Hamilton's pole is his first since the 2023 Hungarian Grand Prix, three years and three months ago, and the 105th of his career.

He is the oldest driver to secure a pole since Mario Andretti for Ferrari at the 1982 Italian Grand Prix.

He and Russell both went out early for their first runs and had to watch as their rivals sought and failed to beat them.

Leclerc went first, falling short of Hamilton by 0.119secs. Antonelli was never on target but Verstappen was fastest of all after two sectors and on course to take pole.

But the Dutchman locked up into the hairpin in the stadium section and ruined his lap.

"Oh man, I'm lost for words," said Hamilton. "It's been a really challenging weekend - we had the engine issue yesterday, which meant we were on the back foot and didn't do a long run.

"We've done a really good job on the setup and to have pole here, wow, it feels special. It's my first pole for Ferrari, and 105th, I like that number.

"To have your first Ferrari pole, it takes me back to watching Michael [Schumacher] get all those poles when he was at Ferrari and all those wins."

Hamilton had been only fourth on the first runs, more than 0.4secs off Leclerc's pace-setting time. But on his final run, he said: "I don't think I lost any time anywhere. It was a super-good lap."

Russell, who said he was happy to have ended a run of difficult form but could not explain why, took a unilateral decision not to do a preparation lap after his out lap on his final run.

He said he had a "gut feeling" that it was the best approach, but the team had insisted on a prep lap and had fuelled the car for the extra mileage.

"[The time loss for the extra fuel weight is] such a small number," said Russell, "but it's bigger than the gap to pole. Nevertheless, I'm just happy to be up here."

Verstappen said traffic with another car is what led to his loss of time.

"Already going into (Turn) 12 I had a car very close to me and I already lost time there with the dirty air," he said.

"And then going into the hairpin, instead of going on the left, I had one car on my right where you normally want to open up the corner. So its a bit of an awkward angle you have to go into the hairpin.

"Plus you lose your reference on the right-hand side where you are constantly looking. It's a difficult corner to get right, that killed my lap. The most promising thing is how we turned it around as in practice I was not that happy and we turned it around, I was in the fight for pole."

McLaren's Lando Norris had looked in contention for pole, fastest in the second session and on the first runs in the final session, when he was third fastest behind Leclerc and Verstappen.

But he failed to improve on his final lap and had to be satisfied fight sixth.

"Just not quick enough that's all," said Norris. "The lap was incredible in Q2 to put me P1. That was very unrealistic in terms of achieving that again in Q3.

"I am pretty happy with P6, can't ask a lot more and pretty happy with the job I did with the car I have."

Red Bull's Isack Hadjar, Racing Bulls pair Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad and Alpine's Pierre Gasly completed the top 10.

Fernando Alonso looked to be in contention for his best qualifying of the year for Aston Martin when he went fastest on his first lap of the session ahead of a number of cars that for most of the season have been ahead of him.

But his engine suffered a water leak in the energy recovery system as he started his second attempt, when he was still lying third, and he was ordered to stop the car on track.

Alonso's frustration after a year of poor performance and reliability from the Honda engine was clear in an interview with the official television channel afterwards, when he said a total of nine words in answer to four questions.

In those words, he confirmed it had been an engine problem, said "it was" a good opportunity and it was "correct" that the car has been looking good all weekend - but that he could not do anything in the race "from the back".

articles.title: Humphrey scores 2 TDs and New Mexico beats San Jose State to remain unbeaten in Mountain West games
articles.summary: (AP) — Scottre Humphrey rushed for two touchdowns and New Mexico beat San Jose State 21-16 on Saturday to win its fifth straight game and remain unbeaten in...
articles.body:
SAN JOSE, Calif. (AP) — Scottre Humphrey rushed for two touchdowns and New Mexico beat San Jose State 21-16 on Saturday to win its fifth straight game and remain unbeaten in Mountain West Conference games.

Humphrey capped two first half drives with 1- and 7-yard scoring runs and the Lobos (7-1, 4-0) led 14-9 at halftime. Toa Fa'avae connected with Cade Keith for a 20-yard touchdown late in the third quarter to go up 21-9.

Tuli Tagovailoa-Amosa cut the lead to five with under 11 minutes left with an 89-yard pick-6 but the Spartans' final four possessions ended twice on downs and twice on interceptions, including Austin Brawley's pick at the New Mexico goal line in the final seconds.

The Spartans' (4-5, 2-3) only offensive points came on three Trajan Sinatra field goals (4-5, 2-3).

Fa'avae threw for 101 yards with a TD but was intercepted three times. Kiefer Sibley rushed for 102 yards on 12 carries.

Luke Weaver threw for 190 yards and was picked off twice for San Jose State, which had just 48 yards rushing. Carson Clark had 91 yards receiving.

The Spartans had won the last four meetings. The Lobos won for the first time at San Jose since 1969 after seven losses and a tie.

San Jose State: Home against Northern Illinois next Saturday.

articles.title: Canelo Alvarez regains WBC super-middleweight title with unanimous decision over Christian Mbilli
articles.summary: RIYADH, Saudi Arabia (AP) — Canelo Alvarez regained the WBC super-middleweight championship on Saturday night, using precise counterpunching and a strong sec...
articles.body:
RIYADH, Saudi Arabia (AP) — Canelo Alvarez regained the WBC super-middleweight championship on Saturday night, using precise counterpunching and a strong second-half performance to defeat Christian Mbilli by unanimous decision.

The judges scored the fight 115-112, 116-111 and 117-110 for Alvarez, who handed Mbilli his first professional defeat. Alvarez improved to 64-3-2, while Mbilli fell to 29-1-1.

Returning for the first time since losing his undisputed championship to Terence Crawford in September 2025, the 36-year-old Mexican became a world champion again.

The victory carried significance beyond the belt. Alvarez faced questions about whether his championship years had ended with the Crawford defeat. Against an unbeaten opponent whose pressure presented a test of his ability to sustain his work, Alvarez put together combinations and found the accuracy to take charge as the fight progressed.

"Oh, it's so difficult to explain," Alvarez said. "It's something unbelievable."

Mbilli's pressure and greater activity made the opening half competitive, particularly as he pushed Alvarez toward the ropes. Alvarez answered with body punches and counters, then began finding greater success in the sixth with a right uppercut and straight right.

The change was in the rhythm of the exchanges. Alvarez increasingly made Mbilli respond to his punches, interrupting the champion's advances with cleaner shots. At times, he lowered his hands and beckoned Mbilli forward, inviting exchanges from positions where he could counter.

An uppercut punctuated Alvarez's seventh round, and he followed with combinations in the eighth. Mbilli's task became more difficult when referee Hector Afu deducted a point for a punch to the back of Alvarez's head.

Alvarez's jab helped him control the 10th. Mbilli continued working to the body and landed right hands in the final round, but Alvarez finished emphatically, wobbling the champion with a late right.

Alvarez credited trainer Eddy Reynoso's instructions to move, box and maintain his jab.

"Do what Canelo do the best. And that's what I did," Alvarez said.

Asked whether Mbilli surprised him, Alvarez said he expected a strong opponent but believed he had limited the champion's offense.

"It's difficult to throw punches with me," he said.

The celebration brought an emotional tribute to Eddy Reynoso and Chepo Reynoso, whom Alvarez credited with shaping his career.

Alvarez's tearful celebration and tight embrace with Eddy Reynoso offered a different image from his composed work inside the ropes. After 12 rounds spent managing Mbilli's pressure, he struggled to describe what becoming a champion again meant. His thanks quickly shifted from the achievement to the people who helped him reach it.

"I'm so proud, so proud of my team," Alvarez said.

He also thanked his family watching from afar and joked that his wife, who could not attend, had told him not to return without the championship.

Alvarez offered no immediate commitment to another opponent.

"I'm gonna rest. I'm gonna keep learning. I'm gonna keep working hard," he said.

In the co-main event, Jaime Munguia survived a sixth-round scare to retain his WBA super-middleweight championship against Nikita Zon. Munguia won by unanimous decision, with scores of 117-111, 117-111 and 116-112, recovering after Zon hurt him to improve to 47-2.

Rafael Espinoza retained his WBO featherweight title with a technical knockout of Ricardo Blandon at 1:22 of the third round. A straight right opened a cut above Blandon's left eye, and the referee stopped the fight on the ringside physician's recommendation. Espinoza improved to 29-0 with 25 knockouts.

Reito Tsutsumi scored two second-round knockdowns before stopping Raymundo Rojas Garcia at 2:27. Tsutsumi improved to 6-0 with five knockouts.

articles.title: Canelo Alvarez keeps career alive with vital win over Christian Mbilli
articles.summary: The Mexican icon outpointed Mbilli to win the WBC super-middleweight title, 13 months after a loss to Terence Crawford
articles.body:
Canelo Alvarez scored a crucial win over Christian Mbilli on Saturday, rebounding from a loss to Terence Crawford after 13 months out of the ring.

Alvarez outpointed Mbilli to take the WBC super-middleweight title from the Cameroonian, earning scorecards of 115-112, 116-111, and 117-110.

Those scores factored in a docked point for Mbilli in round eight, after the champion landed one low blow too many for the referee's liking, but it would have been a comfortable win for Canelo regardless.

The Mexican icon was much more active than he had been in recent performances, starting well and – at times – matching the volume punching of Mbilli, who is known for his activity and had never lost before.

Mbilli, 31, allowed that activity to dip here and there on Saturday, and Canelo, 36, capitalised well. The four-weight world champion varied his shots well, landing hard right hooks early on and mixing in uppercuts in the later rounds.

Canelo appeared emotional afterwards, as he regained super-middleweight gold after losing his undisputed status against Crawford last year.

Crawford claimed all the major belts by outpointing Canelo, before retiring from boxing in December. Upon the American's retirement, Mbilli's interim WBC belt was upgraded.

But the Cameroonian's first defence of the official title ended in disappointment, as Canelo got back to winning ways in Riyadh , which has been subjected to deadly attacks in recent weeks .

The Yemen-aligned Houthis had launched numerous strikes on the Saudi city, injuring hundreds of people and killing more than 20, per local authorities.

Still, Saturday's boxing event went ahead at ANB Arena, where Canelo said after winning: "It's so difficult to explain [my emotions]. It's something unbelievable.

"This feels like my first title, now after 21 years as a professional; 16 years ago I won my first title, now I won the title again. I'm so proud, so proud of my team. [They] made me the champion I am."

"No, [nothing surprised me]. I knew he's a strong fighter, and he didn't throw a lot of punches because it's difficult to throw punches with me. I did perfectly."
